title: Beastkin naming, Akan day-naming and Name-Keeping
summary: Real anchor is Akan day-naming plus the Name-Keeping tradition: a soul-name by birth circumstance, a held name as the last thing that cannot be taken; the soul-name carries an attribute the bearer is expected to embody, and failing it is a strong source of internal shame.
verbatim: Real anchor: Akan day-naming plus the Name-Keeping tradition. Soul-name by birth circumstance, held name as the last thing that cannot be taken.

title: Concord Human naming, medieval byname freezing
summary: Real anchor is medieval European byname freezing: a small given-name pool, byname disambiguation, some bynames frozen into surnames, some still live. Frozen surnames read as urban and chartered; live patronymics read as rural and unchartered.
verbatim: Real anchor: Medieval European byname freezing. Small given-name pool, byname disambiguation, some frozen into surnames, some still live.

title: Dawi naming, Norse dithematic compounding and Finnish phonology
summary: Real anchor is Norse dithematic compounding with Finnish phonology: two-element compound given names from a fixed inventory, patronymic, earned byname. The oath-name is a Dawi-specific fourth slot, audible in the full name or audible in its absence.
verbatim: Real anchor: Norse dithematic compounding with Finnish phonology. Two-element compound given names from a fixed inventory, patronymic, earned byname.

title: Elven naming, Northwest Coast institutional logic
summary: Real anchor is Northwest Coast Indigenous institutional logic: names as heritable property, publicly validated, requiring compensated witnesses, ranked name-holding, names as offices. Content is entirely original; no specific crest, ceremonial or sacred terms from living traditions appear. Avoid generic fantasy Elf naming and Tolkien's specific Quenya/Sindarin phonology.
verbatim: Real anchor: Northwest Coast Indigenous institutional logic. Names as heritable property, publicly validated, requiring compensated witnesses. Ranked name-holding. Names as offices.

title: Goblinoid naming, Germanic compounding with heavy phonotactics
summary: Real anchor is Germanic compounding with heavy phonotactics: a short given name plus a compound byname describing the force that made the person; the compounding follows rules and bynames may be inherited past the point anyone remembers the original event.
verbatim: Real anchor: Germanic compounding with heavy phonotactics. Short given name plus compound byname describing the force that made the person.

title: Mahuo naming, Korean generational syllables and clan-first order
summary: Real anchor is Korean generational syllables (dollimja): family name first, a two-syllable given name sharing a generation syllable across the cohort, a clan seat distinguishing unrelated families sharing a surname. Avoid Chinese wuxia conventions and given-name-first Japanese conventions.
verbatim: Real anchor: Korean generational syllables (dollimja). Family name first. Two-syllable given name with one syllable shared across the whole generation of the lineage. Clan seat distinguishing unrelated families sharing a surname.

title: Yukari naming, Japanese life-stage renaming
summary: Real anchor is Japanese life-stage renaming: childhood name, adult name at coming-of-age, calling name for intimates, true name taboo to speak, posthumous name at death. Avoid modern Japanese casual naming; carry feudal-era court weight.
verbatim: Real anchor: Japanese life-stage renaming. Childhood name, adult name conferred at coming-of-age, calling name used by intimates, true name taboo to speak, posthumous name at death.

title: The Agamalu addition to Moto naming, struck
summary: The Ava-name ceremonial slot the Agamalu Family's Ava ceremony conferred on Moto governance figures, distinct from the name Moto governance itself used for the same individual.
verbatim: The Agamalu addition: The Agamalu Family's naming follows the same Polynesian phonological register but adds a ceremonial slot: the Ava-name, conferred during the Ava ceremony that precedes every Fono session.
notes: Struck by the Inner World Naming Amendment §I, which names this specific subsection ("the Agamalu addition beneath it") alongside the Moto/Satulagi section. Distinct from Filemu Agamalu's own Ava-name (Canon Amendment, R21), which is the Agamalu house's own naming for its own members, not an addition layered onto Moto's naming — the Moto Reversion Ledger (R22) says the Agamalu house "keep Polynesian register, which the amendment never governed," so that row is not struck by this one. Flagged as a real ambiguity in CONFLICTS.md.

title: Celestial Host naming, pending a formal pass
summary: Proposed structure is a function-name plus a rank-suffix plus a permanent Lawbell-name declaring which Archonic principle the Celestial serves; current working names are placeholders pending a full naming pass.
verbatim: Current status: Flagged as needing a full naming pass. Working names (Verantha, Kaethren Vareth, Dazgrim, Urstia) are placeholders.

title: The Holy Sea of Alabaster, Latin ecclesiastical naming
summary: Birth name (Concord Common) plus ordination name (Latin, chosen or assigned at vows) plus locative/title; a documented name in the Testimony archive carries metaphysical weight, and an undocumented person is theologically uncounted.
verbatim: Real anchor: Latin ecclesiastical naming conventions. The Papal naming tradition (a chosen name at elevation, replacing the birth name), monastic naming (a new name at profession of vows), and the specific Latin-compound naming of the late medieval Catholic Church.

title: Satulagi/Moto Polynesian naming, struck
summary: The Satulagi/Moto Polynesian naming system (fa'amatai title system, matai title, personal name conferred by the mother's family, the Moto royal matai as sovereign bloodline title).
verbatim: Satulagi / Moto — Polynesian institutional logic
notes: Struck by the Inner World Naming Amendment §I ("The Polynesian register... dead"), see the R23 series once extracted. The Moto naming register is now Japonic, per the Moto Reversion Ledger (R22).

title: Undaar-Keth/Old Vaross naming, a service record in name form
summary: Given name plus genitive patronymic plus district designation plus, for military personnel, a rank compound that changes with every promotion or demotion, making a Mandate citizen's name a service record; Ironblood Orc citizens carry a hybrid orc-personal-name plus Old Vaross patronymic/district name.
verbatim: This addition specifies Old Vaross as a distinct administrative language with its own naming conventions, separate from the frontier goblinoid naming that the existing guide documents.

title: The Concord Human given-name pool is deliberately small
summary: A deliberately small pool of 30 given names (20 male, 20 female) — repetition is the feature, not the bug — combined with patronymic, occupational, locative or descriptive bynames; in a village of two hundred there will be three of the same given name, and the byname is more real than the given name.
verbatim: Deliberately small. Repetition is the feature, not the bug.
notes: The 40 individual names are reference data (a word bank), not extracted row by row.

title: The Dawi element inventory, 30 morphemes for on-the-fly naming
summary: Thirty fixed-meaning morphemes (endurance, craft, stone/metal, virtue, nature) across five categories, combined two-element with consonant gradation at the join, plus patronymic and earned-byname construction, so a compliant name can be generated in under a minute.
verbatim: Two-element compounds. Either element may occupy either position. Consonant gradation applies at the join.
notes: The 30 individual morphemes are reference data (a word bank), not extracted row by row, consistent with how other packs' lexicon tables are treated.

title: The Satulagi/Moto element inventory, struck
summary: Twenty-five open-syllable Polynesian-register morphemes for generating Moto/Satulagi names.
verbatim: Satulagi / Moto Element Inventory (25 elements)
notes: Struck alongside R20-2-MOTO_POLYNESIAN_STRUCK by the Inner World Naming Amendment §I.

title: The Accord files every practitioner into four flattening fields
summary: The Accord files every practitioner under given name, family or patronymic, culture of origin, rank designation — a bureaucratic act that is also a cultural act, reducing a five-slot Yukari name to three fields or stripping a Dawi oath-name for lack of a slot.
verbatim: The Accord's administrative system files every practitioner under a standardised format: given name, family or patronymic, culture of origin, rank designation.

title: Cross-cultural mispronunciation is characterisation, not error
summary: When a name crosses cultures, the speaker's own phonology imposes itself (a Concord human flattens Dawi consonant gradation, a Dawi stress-accents a Yukari pitch-accent name); these adaptations should appear in dialogue as characterisation, not be treated as typos.
verbatim: When a name from one culture is spoken by someone from another, the speaker's phonology imposes itself. A Concord human cannot produce the Dawi consonant gradation and will flatten it. A Dawi cannot produce the Yukari pitch-accent and will stress-accent instead. A goblinoid speaker will add consonant clusters to Satulagi names that the Satulagi phonotactics do not permit. These adaptations are not errors. They are the reality of names crossing borders, and they should appear in dialogue: a character mispronouncing another character's name is characterisation, not a typo.

title: The Third Name exists outside all cultural naming conventions
summary: The earned Third Name (documented in The Standing and the Title) is conferred in whatever language the naming community speaks and has no equivalent in the bearer's own register; carrying one means one's identity now belongs to the people who named you rather than the people who bore you.
verbatim: The Standing and the Title documents the Third Name: the earned title that the world assigns. The Third Name exists outside all cultural naming conventions.

title: Each culture has different name-change triggers; cross-culture is never clean
summary: Yukari rename at life-stage; Dawi add the oath-name at oath-taking; Elven validate or strip names publicly; Concord freezes bynames into surnames over generations; Beastkin hold name-keeping as a last resort. Which rule applies when a character moves between cultures is always specific to the characters involved and never clean.
verbatim: Each culture has different triggers for name-change. The Yukari rename at life-stage transitions. The Dawi add the oath-name at oath-taking. The Elven validate or strip names publicly. The Concord system freezes bynames into surnames over generations. The Beastkin hold their name-keeping as a last resort. When a character moves between cultures, the question of which naming rules apply produces genuine conflict: does a Mahuo practitioner who swears a Dawi oath gain an oath-name? Does a Concord human adopted into a Yukari household receive a new name at coming-of-age? The answer is always specific to the characters involved, and the answer is never clean.

title: Formal address follows the addressing institution or culture
summary: A practitioner's formal address follows the convention of whoever is doing the addressing (rank plus family name for the Accord, ordination name plus title for Sanctum Lux, relationship-dependent honorifics at a Ketsuen court); two people in the same room may correctly address the same person by different names.
verbatim: A practitioner's formal address follows the convention of the institution or the culture that is doing the addressing.

title: A character is introduced by whatever name the POV would use
summary: Introduce a character by whatever name the POV character would use (formal on first meeting, personal for intimates, Third Name or physical description for strangers); the narrator does not switch names without a reason, since a name-switch is a statement about the character's relationship to the reader.
verbatim: Prose convention: introduce a character by whatever name the POV character would use. A practitioner meeting another practitioner for the first time uses the formal address. An intimate uses the personal name. A stranger uses the Third Name if they have heard it, and a physical description if they have not. The narrator uses the name the scene has established and does not switch without a reason, because a name-switch in narration is a statement about how the character's relationship to the reader has changed.

title: A dominant Third Name consumes the personal name and rank
summary: When a Third Name becomes dominant, both the personal name and institutional rank recede — the title becomes the person, and the birth name is what the family uses and nobody else remembers.
verbatim: When a practitioner's Third Name becomes dominant, the personal name and the institutional rank both recede. Nobody calls Cozbi Mahuo "Grandmaster Mahuo" unless they are reading from a filing. He is The Ledger-Keeper, and the Third Name has consumed the other two. This is the endgame of the naming system: the title becomes the person, the person becomes the title, and the birth name is what the family uses and nobody else remembers.

title: Remaining element-inventory gaps
summary: Remaining gaps after this amendment: Mahuo element inventory, Yukari element inventory, Elven branch-specific element inventories, and Beastkin soul-name inventory.
verbatim: Remaining gaps: Mahuo element inventory, Yukari element inventory, Elven branch-specific element inventories, Beastkin soul-name inventory.
ratified: Isaac, 2026-09-12, Claude Code: yes, fill in the gaps
notes: RULED 2026-09-12: yes, fill them in. Drafted by a background research agent, matching the existing Dawi/Moto inventory format where it fits and restructured where the culture's own anchor doesn't fit that shape (elven branches: shared roots + branch affixes; Beastkin: circumstance + expectation + Name-Keeping, matching the Akan day-name anchor). Several per-inventory items flagged rather than invented where canon doesn't settle a detail. Full draft in proposals/element_inventories_draft.md, logged in proposals/PROPOSED.md. Superseded 2026-09-12 by R37-1-MAHUO_ELEMENT_INVENTORY (with R37-2, R37-3, R37-4 in rules/doc-element-inventories.yaml), Isaac having ratified the draft as written with its open flags kept as flags; the four inventories are published at wiki/The Tongues of the Realms/Element Inventories -- Mahuo, Yukari, the Elven Branches, Beastkin.md.

title: Chinese stratum phonotactics avoid the wuxia register

title: The Chinese stratum's six name slots
summary: Surname (one syllable), generation character (fixed decades in advance by a lineage-hall poem, revealing relative seniority on first exchange), given character (the individual half), courtesy name (taken at capping, adult use — using someone's given name past that point is a superior's privilege or a deliberate insult), studio name (optional, self-chosen, for scholars/physicians/ alchemists), and posthumous name (conferred by the hall, occasionally an insult).
verbatim: Surname. One syllable, effectively always. This alone separates it on sight from the Korean stratum, where the lineage name arrives with a hollow-seat behind it.
ratified: Isaac, 2026-09-11, Claude Code session: ratified by direction ("most of them are ratified"); his standing Natalie project instructions treat this pack as live.

title: Distinguishing the Chinese stratum from the Korean on the page
summary: A hyphen means Mahuo (Korean); no hyphen means the lineage halls (Chinese). A hollow-seat means Mahuo; the halls use the book instead. A courtesy name means the halls; no Mahuo character has one. A two-syllable surname means neither register — that's Japonic.
verbatim: Hyphen means Mahuo. Kwon Mu-jin. No hyphen means the lineage halls.
ratified: Isaac, 2026-09-11, Claude Code session: ratified by direction ("most of them are ratified"); his standing Natalie project instructions treat this pack as live.

title: A carried name is a person, and it survives them
summary: A name is not a label but a person; when someone dies the name is held unspoken until given on to a child, who carries the same name, not a memory or tribute, and is treated accordingly by everyone who loved it.
verbatim: The carried name. A name is not a label attached to a person. It is a person, and it survives them. When someone dies the name is held, unspoken, until it is given on to a child, and the child carries it.
ratified: Isaac, 2026-09-11, Claude Code session: ratified by direction ("most of them are ratified"); his standing Natalie project instructions treat this pack as live.

title: A carried name does not transfer out; giving one is enormous
summary: A Far-Northern child fostered south keeps the carried name but simply stops hearing it used, and the kin-turns lapse; giving a carried name to an outsider makes them a specific dead person, with all the kin-turns, binding the household without individual consent.
verbatim: A carried name does not transfer out. A Far-Northern child fostered south keeps it and simply stops hearing it used, and the kin-turns lapse, and that lapse is one of the quieter griefs available in the setting.
ratified: Isaac, 2026-09-11, Claude Code session: ratified by direction ("most of them are ratified"); his standing Natalie project instructions treat this pack as live.

title: The kin-turn, kinship terms follow the name instead of the blood
summary: A woman whose mother's name is given to her newborn daughter calls that infant "mother," and means it, and the settlement uses the term with her; names are not gendered, and a person may carry several, each bringing its own kin-turn.
verbatim: The kin-turn. Kinship terms follow the name instead of the blood. A woman whose mother's name is given to her newborn daughter calls that infant mother, and means it, and the whole settlement uses the term with her.
ratified: Isaac, 2026-09-11, Claude Code session: ratified by direction ("most of them are ratified"); his standing Natalie project instructions treat this pack as live.

title: Name-avoidance interlocks with Kharven's Waiting
summary: The name of the recently dead is unsayable until given on; the Waiting is the silence — the body waits in the death-house because the ground is frozen, and the name waits with it, leaving a hole in the household's vocabulary that everyone steers around.
verbatim: Name-avoidance. The name of the recently dead is not spoken until it has been given on. This interlocks with the Standing Inventory at no cost: the Waiting is the silence.
ratified: Isaac, 2026-09-11, Claude Code session: ratified by direction ("most of them are ratified"); his standing Natalie project instructions treat this pack as live.

title: Far-Northern phonotactics for coining names
summary: Three vowels (a i u) with phonemic length, uvulars as the signature (q where another register takes k), velar/uvular fricatives, geminate consonants across syllable boundaries, no onset clusters, heavily suffixing with meaningful morphemes, light and late stress.
verbatim: Three vowels, a i u, with phonemic length. Uvulars are the signature: q where another register would take k.
ratified: Isaac, 2026-09-11, Claude Code session: ratified by direction ("most of them are ratified"); his standing Natalie project instructions treat this pack as live.

title: Far-Northern surnames were assigned by the Accord's filing system

verbatim: The Accord's registers cannot file a person who has no fixed name. So the filing system assigned them: a frozen surname taken off the nearest legible thing, a trade, a landmark, a factor's guess at a sound, handed down in a ledger to people who had never used one and mostly still do not among themselves.
ratified: Isaac, 2026-09-11, Claude Code session: ratified by direction ("most of them are ratified"); his standing Natalie project instructions treat this pack as live.

pack: Racial Voice and Dialect Guide Amendment
title: Fleshshaper idiom is anatomy applied to everything; two markers
summary: Anatomy applied to everything, not as metaphor but as their actual vocabulary (a seam, badly sutured, swelling, opened, holds under load); exactly two phonetic markers — dropped final -g on gerunds, and "th" hardening to "d" only in unstressed grammatical positions.
verbatim: Anatomy, applied to everything. Not as metaphor and not as a shock device. It is simply the vocabulary they have, extended outward the way a sailor extends rigging or a smith extends heat.

pack: Racial Voice and Dialect Guide Amendment
title: Fleshshaper signature turns and stress-tell
summary: Signature lines "That closes" (anything settled) and "Who holds it?" (their first question about any structure); under stress they become more procedural, not less, shortening to pure sequence with the reasons dropped.
verbatim: - "That closes." Said of anything settled: a wound, an argument, a debt, a life. Their all-purpose full stop. - "Who holds it?" Their first question about any structure, organisation, alliance or plan.

pack: Racial Voice and Dialect Guide Amendment
title: Fleshshaper syntax fronts the object being worked on
summary: Short declarative clauses in working order, sequence first and reason second or not at all; they front the object ("The arm, I open here"), naming the thing being worked on before the working.
verbatim: Short declarative clauses in working order. They describe procedure the way a competent tradesman describes procedure: sequence first, reason second or not at all. Compound sentences are rare and always join a step to its consequence. They front the object. The arm, I open here.

pack: Racial Voice and Dialect Guide Amendment
title: Winter Eladrin speak; speech is the least of what they do
summary: Winter Eladrin are not silent; speech is the least of what they are doing, and the prose has to carry the rest through distance and stillness.
verbatim: The governing principle: they speak. The convention is not silence. It is that speech is the least of what they are doing, and the prose has to carry the rest.

pack: Racial Voice and Dialect Guide Amendment
title: Eladrin idiom is weather and cold; two signature turns
summary: Idiom draws on weather, season and the behaviour of cold as literal analytical vocabulary (thawing/set, keeps, melted, tracked); signature lines "It keeps" and "You have moved"; under stress stillness increases and the distance grammar stops entirely.
verbatim: Weather, season and the behaviour of cold. Never as decoration and always as the actual analytical vocabulary.

pack: Racial Voice and Dialect Guide Amendment
title: Never write an Eladrin line without a distance/stillness beat
summary: Never write an Eladrin line of dialogue without a distance or stillness beat attached; a bare Eladrin line is an incomplete sentence in their language.
verbatim: Never write an Eladrin line of dialogue without a distance or stillness beat attached. A bare Eladrin line is an incomplete sentence in their language, and the reader should be able to follow an entire Eladrin conversation with the dialogue removed.

pack: Racial Voice and Dialect Guide Amendment
title: Eladrin syntax is archaic-formal with zero phonetic markers
summary: No contractions ever, present tense for permanent conditions, questions phrased as statements with an expectant pause, no interrupting or overlapping; zero phonetic markers, deliberately — their unaccented perfection is enormous effort read as coldness.
verbatim: Formal, complete, and slightly archaic through the retention of full forms: no contractions, ever, and this is the one absolute in the register.

pack: Racial Voice and Dialect Guide Amendment
title: Eladrin communication runs on speech, distance and stillness
summary: Prose must render at least two of three simultaneous channels in any exchange of consequence — sparse speech that rarely carries the content, distance (approach is agreement, a half-step back is objection, turning without moving the feet is refusal), and stillness (complete stillness is often the loudest thing in the room).
verbatim: Winter Eladrin communication runs on three channels simultaneously. Prose must render at least two in any exchange of consequence.

pack: Racial Voice and Dialect Guide Amendment
title: A Host line that scans as a maxim has failed
summary: Any Host line that could appear on a temple wall has failed; if it scans as a maxim, cut it and replace it with a report.
verbatim: Any Host line that could appear on a temple wall has failed. If it scans as a maxim, cut it and replace it with a report.

pack: Racial Voice and Dialect Guide Amendment
title: The Host cannot be imprecise, and knows its precision is useless
summary: A Host gives an answer that is correct and unusable, aware of this and unable to do anything about it — accurate rather than confident, which is what stops them sounding like scripture.
verbatim: They cannot be imprecise, and they know their precision is useless. A Host asked how long something will take gives an answer that is correct and unusable.

pack: Racial Voice and Dialect Guide Amendment
title: The Host reports accurately; accuracy doesn't translate to mortal use
summary: The Host is not speaking scripture; they report accurately, and their difficulty is that accuracy in their register does not translate into a mortal one.
verbatim: The governing principle: they are not speaking scripture. They are reporting, accurately, and their difficulty is that accuracy in their register does not translate into a mortal one.

pack: Racial Voice and Dialect Guide Amendment
title: The Host's idiom is measure and law; obvious celestial words banned
summary: Idiom draws on measure, position and law (out of position, standing, no place, release a claim); light/fire/wings are banned as too obvious; signature lines "That is not the question" and "I do not have that"; under stress the Host becomes more precise and slower, with hedges appearing for the first time.
verbatim: Measure, position, and law. Distance, weight, order, precedence, standing. Never light, never fire, never wings. The obvious celestial vocabulary is banned in this register precisely because it is obvious.

pack: Racial Voice and Dialect Guide Amendment
title: The Host is declarative, unhedged, and answers precisely
summary: Declarative, present tense, unhedged — never "I think" or "perhaps"; short flat subject-verb-object sentences; they answer precisely the question asked, not the question intended, which is where every conversation with the Host goes wrong.
verbatim: Declarative, present tense, and unhedged. The Host does not say I think, perhaps, it seems or in my view, because those constructions describe a relationship between a speaker and a claim, and the Host does not have that relationship. They state.

pack: Racial Voice and Dialect Guide Amendment
title: All three registers are originations, overridden by any prior lore
summary: All three registers are originations contradicting no existing lore (none existed); if any culture has established speech in an unreached document, these are overridden by it.
verbatim: All three are originations and none contradicts existing lore, because no lore existed. If any of these cultures has established speech in a document I did not reach, these are overridden by it and I would rather be told than have it discovered in prose.

pack: Obsession Force / Attraction Path Gate Ruling
title: Obsession Force satisfies an Attraction Path gate
summary: A practitioner whose Attraction Layer runs under Obsession Force — the corrupted inversion of Attraction Force — still satisfies an Attraction Path gate for sub-stat purposes. Obsession does not cap Attraction-gated sub-stats hard; this is a setting-wide mechanical rule covering every corrupted practitioner, not a fix scoped to one character.
verbatim: Does Obsession satisfy an Attraction Path gate? Yes — Isaac's ruling, 2026-09-12. The values below stand, confirmed rather than conditional. He keeps Silence — the man who is quieter than the background stays exactly that. The ruling is general: Obsession Force satisfies an Attraction Path gate for every corrupted practitioner in the setting, not only him.
ratified: Isaac, 2026-09-12, Claude Code: ruled directly, no source document
notes: Raised as an open ruling on wiki/Volume III — Character Cards/Sinclair Mercer · The Soul Devourer.md (Section IV), which explicitly flagged the question as affecting every corrupted practitioner in the setting, not only Sinclair. Isaac ruled yes; Sinclair's sheet was patched in Notion to a resolved statement (his three gate-contested sub-stats -- Dexterity Silence, Ardency Depth, Tempering Capacity -- now read "Gate cleared" and he keeps Silence) and the wiki mirror was re-exported. Checked every other character sheet in wiki/ for the same corrupted-Attraction-Path ambiguity (grep for "Obsession" combined with "Attraction"/"gate"/"Path" across every Volume I-VI Character Cards folder). None carried the same pending-ruling structure as of 2026-09-12: Cozbi Mahuo and Azelra Kaine both run partly or wholly on Obsession Force but neither sheet gates specific sub-stats on an unresolved Path question; Aurelian Prudentius Custos Clausorum's Attraction/Obsession ambiguity is a deliberate unresolved in-world mystery (a standing nine-year Arbitration Division case), not a mechanical gate pending Isaac's ruling. Gorrath Bloodspine's sheet contains one comparison line ("Sinclair loses three sub-stats to the Obsession question") that is now stale phrasing now that the question is resolved in Sinclair's favor; left untouched since Gorrath himself has no Path caps and is not a corrupted Attraction-Path practitioner -- flagged here rather than silently edited, for Isaac or the main session to decide whether it is worth a wording pass.

title: The Concordant Crystal: a general mechanism for a Soul Crystal shared across multiple donors
summary: Establishes the Concordant Crystal as the general, reusable mechanism for a Soul Crystal shared by multiple donors: the Essence Cores stay discrete and take turns at the frame's single, non-multiplying Aether Shell; the Attraction Layer alone runs one Wellspring line per donor; Coherence and eta are pooled off the Shell while Tempering Coherence stays per-donor; the frame runs Overgrown by default; and a donor's death or removal either settles the frame toward Refined or, if the survivors will not release it, curdles into Obsession Force -- a failure mode, like single-Shell collapse, that no single-donor Crystal can suffer.
verbatim:
A Concordant Crystal is the standing mechanism for a Soul Crystal shared across multiple donors. It is Synergia -- several Soul Crystals briefly sharing one Essence Core, Shell and Layer -- made permanent by Concordia instead of left momentary, ordinarily sealed through a Ritus such as the Rite of Hollow Union rather than held open by anyone's ongoing concentration. Formation requires that the donors already carry an Attraction-recognized bond strong enough for the Continuum to read them as one Attraction signature; kinship, oath, or shared catastrophe qualify, strangers do not.
The three layers do not fuse identically. The Essence Cores never fuse: each donor keeps a discrete Core -- identity, memory and Traits remain their own -- and only one donor's Core occupies the frame's single point of outward control at a time, with the hand-off between donors itself a Continuum-recognized cost that degrades Dexterity and Reflex-family Sub-Stats independent of the frame's build. The Aether Shell fuses and is singular without exception: one frame produces exactly one Aether Class, one eta, and one Coherence Band, however many donors it carries, because a body has only one nervous system to conduct through -- a Concordant Crystal does not multiply a Shell's ceiling by donor count, it grants N donors the throughput of one Shell. The Attraction Layer alone is genuinely plural: it carries one discrete Wellspring harmonization per donor, running concurrently rather than blending into a single current, which is how a Concordant Crystal expresses several Wellsprings where a single-donor Crystal expresses at most a compatible few; donors drawing on opposed Wellspring Houses cannot co-anchor one Layer and the frame will not form, or will not hold.
Coherence and eta are pooled, read once off the shared Shell regardless of donor count. Tempering Coherence, the Sub-Stat, stays per-donor because it lives in the Essence Core; a Concordant Crystal's stability is read off its least coherent donor, not their average. A Concordant Crystal runs Overgrown by default, not as a symptom: one Shell built to one donor's architecture now carries the combined Essence pressure of every donor it holds.
A donor's death or clean removal drops the frame from N to N-1 donors without destroying it: that donor's Wellspring line falls silent, the Shell re-equilibrates, and the frame settles toward Refined as the shed pressure eases its standing Overgrowth. A death the surviving donors refuse to release does not settle; the bond curdles into Obsession Force instead of dissolving, and the frame fractures under a signature that has stopped answering. A Concordant Crystal carries two failure modes no single-donor Crystal can suffer: Obsession Force fixation on an unreleased co-donor, and total loss of output from every donor at once should the single shared Shell Cloud or Rupture, where separate Crystals would each fail independently.
ratified: Isaac, 2026-09-12, Claude Code: write the mechanism -- a shared/split Soul Crystal is now a real, documented setting-wide thing, not a one-off exception just for this one Choir.
notes: Originated 2026-09-12 (no source document -- Isaac's ruling was to write the mechanism itself). Resolves the open ruling previously flagged on wiki/Volume IV — Character Cards/The Ossuary Choir.md ("there is no mechanism in Fracture of Worlds for a shared Soul Crystal across three donors"); that card has been edited in Notion to carry this mechanism under its own §II and its wiki mirror re-exported. Grounded in Synergia and Concordia (wiki/The Magic System/The Magical Categories — Unified Taxonom.md) and in the standard Essence Core / Aether Shell / Attraction Layer split (wiki/The Magic System/The Core Vocabulary.md, wiki/The Magic System/Tier Grade, Bands & the Aether Shell.md). Written general-purpose: applies to any future multi-donor Soul Crystal, not only the Ossuary Choir, which serves here only as the worked example (three donors, three Wellsprings -- Dissolution and Nihiloth sharing the Limina House, Calcination running Caloria alongside them).

title: Cymorath is the Air of Ascent; frost and stasis are Vohrin, Caloria, Thermodynamics
summary: Cymorath carries exactly the portfolio Fracture of Worlds gives it: the Air of Ascent, Family Fulguria, freedom and motion, strengthening Dexterity Celerity and Gnosis Cartography/Perception. It is not a frost Wellspring. Every frost, cold or stasis working the wiki had been drafting as Cymorath is keyed instead to Vohrin, the Abyssal Depths Titan, Family Caloria, Physics Domain Thermodynamics, on the FOW III reading that cold is heat run backward. There is no dedicated frost Wellspring. Codex lines, Wellspring harmonisation rows and Material Ledger resonance columns that name a cold law write Vohrin · Caloria · Thermodynamics; any surviving Cymorath usage is Fulguria.
verbatim: re-homed on Vohrin, the Abyssal Depths Titan that FOW III already names as the thermal-extraction signature: Family Caloria, Physics Domain Thermodynamics, Titan-keyed. Cymorath is the Air of Ascent exactly as Fracture of Worlds gives it, freedom and motion, Dexterity Celerity and Gnosis Cartography and Perception, and nothing else. Nothing on the FOW canon pages changes. This entry drafted its own cold out of Caloria and touched neither, and the ruling says that was the right shape: there is no dedicated frost Wellspring, cold is heat run backward, and the pages that had been calling it Cymorath now call it Vohrin.
ratified: Isaac, 2026-09-12, Claude Code: ruled directly, no source document
notes: Raised as an open ruling on wiki/Summoned and Bound/Haelvorn · Housecat.md (Section XIII), whose blockquote recorded the spelling ruling and flagged the portfolio clash it exposed. Isaac ruled the same day; the blockquote was rewritten in Notion to a resolved statement (the verbatim above is quoted from it) and the mirror re-exported. Retagged to Vohrin · Caloria · Thermodynamics in Notion, mirrors refreshed: Hide, Horn and Bone (Fellstag Winterpelt, Coldblood Concentrate); The Arctic Lion — Sovereign Configuration (header, Aethersteel, Frost Array, Glacium, three-node architecture and every frost technique's Codex line); Bloodbind Surge; Hunter's Breath; Maw of Crystalline Stasis; Vorynn Execution Strike; Winter Rend; The Old World — The Western Wearing (Glacium); The Abyssal Depths (The Stillwater Rite's Codex); The Alchemical Index (Stasisline Needles, Stillwater Draught); The Material Index T5–T9 (Glacium, Frostwool); and the Draven Kael Vorrick, Kaelen Brighthoof, Vaelthyr Iscarn and Valthrum · The Cryon King cards. Left as Cymorath because the usage is motion, vector-field, wind or vibration reading rather than cold: the FOW V and Fulguria canon pages, Niran Yukari, Ryuka Yukari, Lucius Xenotro, Rengai Zettari, Mizuki Moto (vibration through frost mist, not the frost itself), Azhura Vyren, Karu Velnar, Liorien Nael-Teth, Vaelorian Theryn Aerethiel, Iryen Maevith, The Reach Dwarves, Nadi, The Sage Arts, Hataraki, Kami no Kobushi, Ketsuen, Celestial Harmonic Shear, Harmonic Null-Ascension, Radiant Ribbon Shell, The Crossing and the Making of the God Hand, and the Niran scenes. Judgment calls: the Arctic Lion sheet's Fulguria-match row now states that the Family match runs through the Judicium substrate and the frost layer is Caloria; whether a Caloria layer inside a Fulguria structure carries a §14 stress figure the way the Ruins layer does is not ruled and was not invented. Stasisline Needles (rate arrest, no frost) was read as stasis and retagged; Cryost Ascendant, Mizuki Moto and Draven's Identity line already routed frost through Vohrin and were the model.

title: The black stones are an analogue of Crevice Shale, not Crevice Shale
summary: The black stones that fell across four worlds when Verinus completed the Void are Voidfall Stone, a distinct T8 material: matte, made not emplaced, and indistinguishable from Crevice Shale to Measurewright instruments at a distance. They are not Crevice Shale. Article III names Crevice Shale specifically and does not name Voidfall Stone, so Enforcement acting under Article III against the stones is acting on a misreading; write it that way. Never put the word "shale" on the narrative page of the Verinus scenes for these stones. The Crevice Shale ledger rows stand unchanged.
verbatim: Reads as Crevice Shale to a Measurewright's instruments at a distance, and no instrument yet tells the two apart. Not found. Made, when the Void was completed, and what is completed has weight. Whether it acts on Realm law as Shale does is not recorded. Article III names Crevice Shale and does not name this. Enforcement cannot currently tell them apart, and Enforcement has hanged eleven men under Article III without once being asked to explain the sentence. An analogue of Crevice Shale, not Crevice Shale. Article III's wording is now tested
ratified: Isaac, 2026-09-12, Claude Code: ruled directly, no source document
notes: Verbatim is the "What it is" cell of the Voidfall Stone row on wiki/The Master Material Ledger/The Material Index · T5–T9.md (T8 band; Notion table_row 3d958200-eb22-81ed-8ba2-eb665a8e3b34), plain text with the bold/italic markup stripped. Behaviour in the row is limited to what the scenes show: matte, "taking the light and giving nothing back", none larger than a loaf, cracked the night-stone beside a Kharven woodpile (02:125); no instrument to read them and no Measurewright to say "shale" (02:129); eleven on the Deepvein station floor with every sealed instrument in the lower vaults at a reading no watchman could account for (06:103). Whether it fractures Realm law as Shale does is deliberately left unrecorded. The Crevice Shale row on the same page carries one appended italic cross-reference to the new row; its own text is unchanged, as are the Shale entries on the Master Material Ledger, the Southern Pan, the Four Ceilings, the Concordance of Ages and the Eight Families pages. Scene 02 note 2 rewritten to a resolved statement; scenes 03:33 and 06:103 are prose using the stones and carry no flag, so untouched. Name chosen in the ledger's own register of plain formation-names (Starcall Pearl, Moonblight Ore, Fatesunder Cord): "Voidfall" states the source and the event and keeps "shale" out of the name, since the point of the ruling is that the stones are not shale and the word is the misreading.

title: A Sacrament or Transposition anchor is a soul holding the celebrant's name at weight, fixed by declaration inside the rite
summary: A Sacrament or Transposition anchor is a soul that holds the celebrant's name at weight, and it is fixed by the celebrant's declaration inside the rite, regardless of whether the anchor consents; the declaration, not consent, is the mechanism, and the bond is held under Fixatio, the anchoring law. It does not lapse when the celebrant leaves the world, the celebrant cannot amend it afterward, and it is not a displaceable affinity bond, so it has no release valve. Transposition.md says nothing about how an anchor bond ends; this rule is silent on ending.
verbatim: Ruled 2026-09-12: the bond is anchored on Aurelian's soul holding Verinus's name at weight, which is the Rubric's own definition of an anchor, fixed by declaration inside the dawn rite ("Do you consent." / "No." / "Entered."), and consent is not the mechanism, the declaration is. It holds under Fixatio, the anchoring law, with no release valve, because it is not a displaceable affinity bond; taking Aurelian here without asking stands as written.
ratified: Isaac, 2026-09-12, Claude Code: ruled directly, no source document
notes: General-purpose rule; the Verinus/Aurelian dawn Sacrament (scenes 01-05 of the Verinus/Aurelian arc) is the worked example, not the scope. What the text gives: (1) the anchor definition is the Rubric on Transposition as quoted at the threshold of scenes/02 ("The anchor is a soul that holds the celebrant's name at weight and will hold it while he is not in his place. The rite does not care whether the anchor has been asked."); (2) the fixing is the declaration made inside the rite (scenes/01: "From this hour the surety is the Palatine's. Your four and your room." then "Do you consent." / "No." / "Entered."; scenes/04: "the office would not permit the amendment, because the anchor had been declared at the third clause and a declaration made inside a rite is a fact about the world"); (3) the holding law is Fixatio, which wiki/Spellcraft/Transposition.md names as the rite's secondary harmonisation "for the Anchor Constructs the card itself says the rite is dangerous to attempt without", and whose law per Fracture of Worlds V is "What is held by Fixatio stays held". Persistence: the line stays tied when the celebrant leaves the world, becomes the wall of an Entombment, and is taken up with the seal (scenes/03 "It would stay tight."; scenes/04 "The line to Aurelian came up with the hand and stayed tied."). On ending: Transposition.md contains no dissolution or release clause for an anchor bond; its only duration language is that "the rite holds only while the officiant's attention and the coupling both hold", which describes the transposition itself stranding on failure, not the anchor bond releasing, and the scenes narrate the bond surviving the officiant's departure from the world. The rule is therefore silent on ending: nothing in the text ends it, and no ending is invented here. Distinguished from the Wellspring-of-Grace gloss in scenes/01 ("a rival bond of higher affinity displaces the existing bond"): that is Benediction's affinity-competition failure mode and does not apply to a Fixatio-held anchor, which is the "not a displaceable affinity bond" clause of the ruling. Flagged, not resolved: Aurelian's Volume I card trait "Nothing Reaches Him In Time" says no working "that requires a completed act to bind can bind him"; this ruling reads the anchor as fixed by the celebrant's declaration, not by any completed act of the anchor's, so the two are consistent on their face, but the card trait was not amended and the reading is recorded here rather than written into the trait. The three scene flags were resolved in place and one Spirit Axes line recording the bond was added to each of Verinus VII's and Aurelian's Volume I cards in Notion, mirrors re-exported.

title: [Abys] Deep is attested at Oblation and Fluxia
summary: The Master Codex row for [Abys] Deep now lists Oblation among its attested Wellsprings and Fluxia among its attested Families, so a Codex assignment line drafting [Abys] on an Oblation-primary, Fluxia construct is legal as written. Its Primary Wellspring, Family and Physics Domain (Abyntheus, Fulguria, Electromagnetism) are unchanged, and [Th] Foundation is not amended and stays cross-family.
verbatim: [Abys] Deep · Oblation and Fluxia added. Ruled 2026-09-12. [Abys] Deep, a directional undertow of sub-Realm pressure, carried an Abyntheus, Fulguria, Electromagnetism row. Its All Attested Wellsprings field now includes Oblation and its All Attested Families field now includes Fluxia, taken on the pitch in Obrenkael · The Mule (Summoned and Bound), Deadweight, on the reasoning that a psychopomp's road is a directional undertow of sub-Realm pressure and that Abyntheus and Oblation are both pressure-grammar Wellsprings under different Archons. Primary Wellspring, Family and Physics Domain are unchanged. [Th] Foundation, drafted beside it in the same chain, is not amended and stays cross-family.
ratified: Isaac, 2026-09-12, Claude Code: ruled directly, no source document
notes: Raised as an open ruling on wiki/Summoned and Bound/Obrenkael · The Mule.md (Section XIII), where Deadweight's chain [Ob] · [Abys] · [Th] was flagged because neither [Abys] Deep nor [Th] Foundation was attested at Oblation in the Master Glyph Index. Isaac took the amendment for [Abys] only. Recorded in three places, all in Notion and re-exported: the Amendments section added to the Master Glyph Index page (wiki/The Magic System/The Master Glyph Index — 136 Attested Forms.md, the text quoted in `verbatim`); the Deadweight Codex Assignment line on the Mule's card ("Amended 2026-09-12: [Abys] Deep's Master Codex row now carries Oblation among its attested Wellsprings and Fluxia among its attested Families"); and the card's Section XIII paragraph, now "Codex amendment taken." The Haelvorn · Housecat cross-reference that pointed at the pitched-not-taken state was updated in the same pass. Deadweight stands as drafted, is not rebuilt, and remains the summon roster's one cross-family chain. `kind` is `definition` rather than `amendment` because the rule schema's kind enum has no `amendment` value and the checker is not to be changed; the row defines what [Abys] Deep's attested lists now read, which is what R25-1 (the other direct ruling of this shape) also files as a definition.

title: The Zettari keep their Swahili/Bantu/Arabic register; carved out of the Japonic stratum
summary: The Zettari bloodline's names, titles and technique names are built in a Swahili/Bantu/Arabic-flavoured register, and that register stands. The five-strata naming convention's assignment of "archaic bloodlines" to the Japonic stratum does not reach the Zettari: they are their own register, a carve-out, not a repeal. The Japonic assignment continues to govern every other archaic line (Moto, Yukari, Yuno).
verbatim: The Zettari speak their own tongue. Their names and their arts are Swahili, Bantu and Arabic in flavour — Kafa-Karim, Habl Flow-Bind, Sarmad Fracture, Sukun Maji, Dawam Soul-Still Art, Kumi-na-Mbili Seal; Zuberi, Ma'Kovu, N'Kharu, Malani, Jomari, N'Yari, Zembari — and that register stands. The five-strata naming convention assigns the archaic bloodlines to the Japonic stratum; the Zettari are carved out of it as a register of their own, and the Japonic assignment continues to govern every other archaic line. Ruled by Isaac, 2026-09-12.
ratified: Isaac, 2026-09-12, Claude Code: ruled directly, no source document (closes C-006)
notes: Closes CONFLICTS.md C-006. The clash was between the five-strata rule as ratified (R23-2-JAPONIC_STRATUM, "Japonic. Archaic Bloodline institutional logic", restated in imports/BRIEFS/common.md) and the Zettari's documented vocabulary on wiki/The Archaic Bloodlines/The Zettari.md and wiki/Factions, Bloodlines & Institutions/The Eight Great Houses of Kushara.md. Isaac ruled the rule gives way. R23-2 stays live and unsuperseded: this row narrows its reach by one bloodline rather than striking it. The verbatim is the Register note added to The Zettari wiki page in Notion on 2026-09-12 (Culture section), mirrored to wiki/. The five-strata statement in imports/BRIEFS/common.md and the 2026-09-12 edition of the Character Naming Guide carry the same carve-out. Companion ruling the same day: C-005, the bloodline is spelled Zettari (not Zettai) everywhere; sources/ still spell it Zettai in the Pack One combat-assignment rows, so those rows' verbatim fields keep the old spelling as a known divergence.

title: Agano Sand and the Witnessed Temper, the Zettari forge culture as a Vow Clause application
summary: The Zettari forge culture answers "what makes a thing trustworthy?" with witness and inheritance, not time: a Zettari-forged object is declared reliable once, before a witness older than the speaker, and the bloodline's Material Covenant Resonance holds the declaration in place. The substrate is Agano Sand ("covenant", Swahili-derived, inside the Zettari's own register), a working measure of the Paths' sand -- condensed lineage memory -- folded into the quench. It is access-gated rather than time-gated: it must come from, or through, someone the Paths already recognize. The rite is the Witnessed Temper, a Vow Clause working and not new magic: at the quench the smith or the sovereign the piece is for speaks a bound claim over the object before a Stone Witness (a ruin, an ancestral hall, a Path-linked relic), and the claim becomes a standing law the object runs. Write it as witnessed law, set against the Dawi's brewed endurance; the cross-culture parallel slot is deliberately left open.
verbatim: A Vow Clause working, not a new kind of magic. At the quench, the smith — or the sovereign the piece is being made for — speaks a bound claim over the object before a Stone Witness: a ruin, an ancestral hall, a Path-linked relic. Per the Stone Witness Oath, it must be something older than the speaker. That claim becomes a standing law the object runs, exactly as a spoken vow becomes a standing law a Soul Crystal runs.
ratified: Isaac, 2026-09-12, Claude Code: ratified as written
notes: Answers Docket 18 (R2/R3/R4-OP-ZETTARI_DOCKET, "the oldest unaddressed gap in the project"), which Isaac ruled should be drafted as a pitch mirroring the Dawi's Cask-Oath approach. Built only on lore already on record: Material Covenant Resonance and the Stone Witness Oath (The Zettari hub), the Paths' sand as condensed lineage memory and its lineage-acknowledged entry gate (The Paths), and the Vow Clause as the setting's one general oath-magic mechanism (The Magical Categories). Published 2026-09-12 as a child page of The Zettari hub, mirroring the Moto Material Culture precedent (R34) rather than the Dawi's inline subsection, because the ratified text is too long for the hub's Culture list; the hub's Culture section gained a one-line pointer after the Stone Witness Oath entry and the Register note ruled the same day was left untouched. Item-level consequences and the trade entry are R33-2.

title: What a Witnessed-Tempered item does, what breaks it, and its trade entry
summary: A Witnessed-Tempered piece inherits a scaled-down Ancestral Dominion Frame: every significant strain it survives in the hands of whoever it was sworn to makes it measurably more resistant to that same kind of stress thereafter, and the hardening plateaus the way the bloodline's own combat maturity does. If the piece changes hands outside the terms of the oath its accrued memory does not transfer -- the cost falls on the object's recognition of the new holder, not on the oath-breaker's Crystal Coherence as with the Dawi -- and in the worst documented cases Physical Plane Authority's "hold shape" reverses for that bearer alone, making the piece more failure-prone in their hands than an ordinary equivalent. Trade entry, Standing Index format: Agano Sand, T4, provenance restricted, Class III / Fidelity A / Carry 26, price 26.0; sourcing requires a lineage-acknowledged Zettari's sponsorship, and no smith outside Kushara has explained why the sand only "listens" to a claim spoken over stone older than the speaker.
verbatim: If the piece changes hands outside the terms of the oath, its accrued memory does not transfer. This is not the Dawi's Crystal-Coherence self-punishment, a cost paid by the oath-breaker's own soul; it is closer to the Weight of the Blood, where failure feels ancestral rather than personal. The object simply stops recognizing the new holder as a party the law was made for. In the worst documented cases, Physical Plane Authority's "hold shape" reverses for that bearer alone, and the piece becomes more failure-prone in their hands than an ordinary equivalent.
ratified: Isaac, 2026-09-12, Claude Code: ratified as written

title: The Moto crown-line dress pattern and the court-versus-campaign split
summary: Moto (Kōkan crown-line) dress is six elements worn together -- red enamel fired over deliberately blackened steel (the Ashen Crown's garnet-on-black-iron palette at human scale); a beast-face boss in the same near-black steel, lion or dragon for the crown-line, at the belt clasp at court and on a shoulder rivet or pauldron on campaign; a knotwork belt that is native-Kharven and not Moto in origin, always a specific inherited or married-in piece; a heavy northern fur mantle over the robe at court, reduced to a collar or lining in the field; and a fitted war-harness worn under a robe open enough to show it -- organised on a court-versus-campaign split that is two priority sets wearing the same lineage markers, never one outfit with accessories added or removed. Write a Moto as magistrate and combatant at once.
verbatim: The crown-line pattern is six things worn together: red enamel over dark steel, a beast-face boss, a knotwork belt, a fur mantle, a robe-over-harness silhouette, and a split between court dress and campaign dress that never collapses into one outfit with the accessories taken off. The pattern in full belongs to Kōkan. The other six Great Lines carry it in their own metal and palette, set out below.
ratified: Isaac, 2026-09-12, Claude Code: ratified as written, including the two flagged items
notes: Closes R21-5-MATERIAL_CULTURE_PENDING (rules/doc-agamalu-buri-origin.yaml), whose proposed elements this adopts unchanged and builds out. The page grounds each element in what was already on record: the Ashen Crown's "ironwork set with garnet" (The Kingdom of Kharven — The Ashen Crown), Muken's Crown Mantle of Kharven and Sodoku's Field Coat (Volume I cards), Artemis Amagiri Moto's Passbreaker Mantle as the one prior campaign-worn over-robe, and the Concord baseline's quenched-dark finish and wholeness-marks-rank rule (The Apparatus of the Age). title: Material-culture variations for the other six Great Lines
summary: Only Kōkan holds a seat and is the only line entitled to the full court presentation without it reading as a claim on the throne; the other six Great Lines are landless and their dress is portable, worn-on-the-body wealth carrying the crown-line pattern in their own metal and palette -- Shirogane in bright, hard silver; Akagane in copper and red-bronze fittings with no enamel; Kurenai in unrelieved black and ash-grey with the crimson kept to a single hidden accent; Byakuya in pale near-white with an almost ecclesiastical cut; Tenrai in gold and imperial-toned trim with banner-heraldry in place of a boss; Amagiri in indigo and mist-grey, lighter and less armoured than the rest. The Tenrai palette and the Kurenai crimson/black contrast are canon, not speculative.
verbatim: Only Kōkan holds a seat. The other six Great Lines are landless since the western seat's fall, and their material culture is portable, worn-on-the-body wealth rather than the fixed authority Kōkan expresses through a literal crown and a literal seat. Each of the six carries the pattern in its own metal and palette: Shirogane in bright silver, Akagane in copper and red-bronze, Kurenai in black and ash with the crimson hidden, Byakuya in near-white, Tenrai in gold and banner-heraldry, Amagiri in indigo and mist-grey.

title: Three narration registers define psychic distance per POV character
summary: Every POV character carries one of three narration registers — close (narration fuses with the character's own idiom, italicized direct thought available), medium (POV locked, no head-hopping, but emotion arrives by external behaviour or simile, no italicized thought) or distant/formal (an omniscient epigrammatic voice describes the character from outside, occasional aphoristic italics, the one register licensed for more narratorial explanation) — and the field is called "narration register", never "Band", because Band is the unrelated FOW Coherence stat. This supplies the whose-idiom input that R4-13-FID_CARVEOUT depends on.
verbatim: Every POV character carries a narration register: how far the narration stands from the character's own idiom in that character's POV scenes. There are three. - Close register. Narration fuses with the character's own idiom. Sustained italicized direct thought is available, and even non-italic narration stays inside the character's trained vocabulary. The narration can be wrong the way the character is wrong. - Medium register. POV stays with the character and never head-hops, but emotion arrives via external behavioral description or simile rather than a fused personal idiom. No italicized direct thought. - Distant/formal register. An omniscient, epigrammatic narratorial voice describes the character from outside, with only occasional aphoristic italics. The distance is itself characterization, and it is the one register licensed for more narratorial explanation than the others get. The field is called "narration register", not "Band". The Fracture of Worlds magic system already uses "Band" for a different, unrelated stat (Coherence Band A–F), and the two should never appear interchangeably in the same sentence.
ratified: Isaac, 2026-09-12, Claude Code: ratified as written
notes: Closes the open item R4-OP-PSYCHIC_DISTANCE_BANDS (Pack Four, Still Open), which said FID is house default but no character has a specified band and that Amendment Thirteen's carve-out (R4-13) depends on knowing whose idiom the narration runs in. Two amends loci because the R4-OP row itself carried amends: null and the FID licence these registers parametrise lives in both guides: the Master Style Directive §1.1 is where free indirect discourse is licensed (Pack Five C.3 cites "Directive Sec. 1.1" for it, and R5-C3 amends that locus), and R4-13-FID_CARVEOUT, the rule these registers feed, amends the Scene Writing Process Guide §6 (desktop/NATALIE.md also files "POV lock, psychic distance" under that guide). TERM COLLISION, recorded not resolved: Pack Five C.3 (R5-C3-NARRATION_REGISTER_EXTENSION, live, demoted to flavour by R15-1) already uses "narration registers" for per-culture diction (Dawi / Eresse / Concord human / Moto POV) and its cross-reference keeps "band" (psychic distance) and "register" (culture) as two things to be "assigned together". Isaac ratified the draft's naming as written, so this row's "narration register" means the psychic-distance axis; where both senses could be read, say "narration register (psychic distance)" or "culture register". Logged in CONFLICTS.md. The published text is docs/NARRATION_REGISTERS.md (repo) and the Notion page "Narration Registers — Psychic Distance by POV" under The Rule Index, recorded in build/.notion_publish.json.

pack: Yasoshima Essence Sink / What House Yuno Declined to Disclose
section: What the Research Division Was Not Told
title: Yasoshima's Essence stability is a House Yuno sink, worked by the Kagura branch at cost
summary: Yasoshima's Essence stability is not natural. For two hundred thousand years House Yuno's Kagura branch has used the island as a sink, gathering and metabolising the world's ambient Essence drift one convergence rite at a time through the deepest reach of Tōbō no Michi; the ore-less islands are the right vessel because nothing in them distorts what is poured in. The working is paid for: the Kagura officiants who hold each convergence spend a sliver of their own selfhood into the pattern (Ritual Self-Dilution, the cost Ayame's own card names for her single-city version at Kharven). The house refuses the Research Division because an outside apparatus measuring the sink changes what it is holding (Kiyome's bar on profane or unstable use), because a partial account is itself a badly formed act, and because the mechanism is the only leverage that has kept the island unconquered. Consequence hook if forced open: the load backs up and discharges violently at Yasoshima, a mainland Measurewright reading spikes for the first time in recorded history, the island becomes the most contested ground in the four quarters, and the house's silence recoils on whoever breaks it like a sealed vow. Reader's knowledge only; no character outside the Kagura officiant line knows it.
verbatim: It is stable because House Yuno has spent two hundred thousand years making it a drain. Every fracture, every fanning-out of chaotic Essence that the rest of the four quarters absorbs and calls weather — the ordinary drift that keeps Measurewrights employed everywhere else in the world — the Kagura branch has been quietly gathering to itself and metabolising, one convergence rite at a time, through the deepest reach of Tōbō no Michi. Yasoshima does not merely tolerate Essence better than anywhere else. It is where a portion of the world's disorder goes to stop being disorder.
ratified: Isaac, 2026-09-12, Claude Code: ratified as written
notes: Answers R21-5-RESEARCH_DIVISION_PENDING (now superseded). Draft: proposals/research_division_secret_draft.md; Isaac ratified it as written on 2026-09-12 (RULINGS.md, "Five proposals ratified wholesale"). Written for Yasoshima / House Yuno per the same-day C-004 ruling; no Wadatsumi, Vāimoana or Agamalu material carried. The Yuno Bloodline page under The Archaic Bloodlines mirrors the "declined four times without explanation" line and was deliberately left untouched (another agent was editing that folder); it still reads as the in-world, unexplained refusal, which is correct for a secret. `amends.guide` names the wiki page the text lives on, following the R31 ("The Master Codex") and R-shared-soul-crystal ("The Ossuary Choir (character card)") precedent for rulings that amend a wiki page rather than a craft guide; The Kingdom of Kharven page was not amended and so is not listed.

title: Mahuo element inventory, breath, soul and the Ledger
summary: A Mahuo given name is two syllables drawn from a fixed thirty-element inventory in five categories (breath and soul, Ledger and record, house and clan-seat, precision and correction, care and healing); one syllable is the generation-syllable shared across a cohort, the other is personal, either may take either position, and the family name may precede or follow since canon attests both orders. Which syllable is generational in the attested pairs, and whether Kwon is a Mahuo cadet branch, stay open flags.
verbatim: Two-syllable given names built from a fixed inventory. One syllable is the generation-syllable, shared by every child of one generation within a line; the other is the personal syllable. Either syllable may occupy either position — canon shows both "Ara Min" and "Mu-jin" orderings. Family name attaches per the existing pattern; canon shows it both preceding (Kwon Mu-jin) and following (Cozbi Mahuo) the given name, and this inventory does not resolve which is "correct" — both are attested.
ratified: Isaac, 2026-09-12, Claude Code: ratified as written, open flags kept as flags

The full inventory (thirty elements, worked example, open flags) is on the wiki page named in the file header; the flags there (generational syllable in Ara/Min and Mu/Jin; Kwon as cadet branch or unrelated clan) were ratified as flags and are not resolved by this row.

title: Yukari element inventory, thread, fate and the crow
summary: A Yukari name is a two-element compound drawn from a thirty-element inventory in five categories (thread and fate, crow and silence, divine and dream, water/stone/grief, weight and office), and a full name carries up to five life-stage forms: childhood name, adult name taken at the Telling, calling-name, taboo true name, posthumous name. Only Ketsu, En, Jin and Mu are canon-attested; the rest are coined to the register. Whether individuals carry a second topographic surname beside "Yukari" stays an open flag.
verbatim: Two-element compounds. A full name carries up to five life-stage forms: childhood name, adult name (taken at the Telling), calling-name (used by intimates), true name (taboo — spoken only among family or before Senri's stone), and posthumous name.
ratified: Isaac, 2026-09-12, Claude Code: ratified as written, open flags kept as flags
notes: Yukari is the register name in force as of 2026-09-12 (Tyurkia was swept to Yukari the same day). The open flag on the page -- whether a Yukari individual carries a second, compound-topographic surname alongside "Yukari" or whether "Yukari" absorbed that function -- was ratified as a flag and is not resolved by this row.

title: Elven branch element inventory, shared roots and branch affixes
summary: The five elven branches (Eressean, Varrisak, Drow, Eladrin, Echo Elves) share one root inventory and one affix inventory drawn from the Vey-Elarin grammar, plus one new branch-specific root each (kalen, sova, morel, faelo, verath); roots are disyllabic and open with restricted codas and every element carries a pitch contour. Branch divergence is shown on the same root, not by five separate lists. The root marin stays unglossed, and the clash with already published apostrophe-style Eressean-adjacent names stays an open flag.
verbatim: Roots are disyllabic and open, codas restricted to a vowel, a liquid (l/r), a nasal (m/n/ny), or th. Every element carries a grammatical pitch contour (level/rising/falling).
ratified: Isaac, 2026-09-12, Claude Code: ratified as written, open flags kept as flags
notes: The branches are named by language, not by quarter; the page says nothing about where they sit, so today's placement of the elven branches in the New World's elven old-ground is neither restated nor contradicted here. Two flags ratified as flags: (1) marin is attested with no gloss anywhere in canon and is left unglossed; (2) the amendment warns against apostrophe-style Elf naming while Volume V/VI characters such as Vaelorian Theryn Aerethiel and Argen Vael'thar use exactly that style, so this inventory reads differently from some names already on the page. Neither is resolved by this row.

title: Beastkin soul-name inventory, circumstance, expectation and Name-Keeping
summary: A Beastkin soul-name is a circumstance-element (how the birth went, Akan-day-name style) spoken together with an expectation-element (the attribute the child is charged to grow into, flavoured by lineage stat), and the held-name is whichever fragment survives when home, rank and kin are gone; a third layer supplies the Name-Keeping ritual vocabulary. Whether the four non-Fox lineages actually practise Name-Keeping, and whether soul-name and held-name are one name or two, stay open flags.
verbatim: A soul-name has two parts spoken together: the circumstance-element (what the birth was like, Akan-day-name style) and the expectation-element (the attribute the child is charged to grow into). The held-name is whichever fragment survives when everything else — home, rank, kin — has been taken.
ratified: Isaac, 2026-09-12, Claude Code: ratified as written, open flags kept as flags
notes: Shaped as three linked layers rather than the Dawi/Moto flat category list because the amendment's own Beastkin anchor is a fixed circumstance-to-name correspondence, not a combinable phoneme pool. Two flags ratified as flags: (1) Name-Keeping is documented only for the Fox-Spirit/Mishiro lineage and the amendment's generalisation to all five is followed, not confirmed; (2) "soul-name by birth circumstance, held name as the last thing" is treated as one name under two descriptions, flagged in case two distinct names were intended. title: The four Percussion moves
summary: The Settling breaks stance (descending full weight into the base); the Sweep breaks the base (horizontal, full arc and mass); the Shove breaks measure (haft/shoulder/boss/pommel at closed distance); the Return breaks recovery (the rebound redirected into a second strike) and is the grammar's signature.

title: Blade hunts openings; Percussion hunts fatigue
summary: A swordsman asks where you are unguarded; a hammer asks where you are already carrying load — fatigue accumulates and openings do not, so percussion fights get more dangerous the longer they run while blade fights get less decisive.
verbatim: Blade grammar hunts openings. Percussion grammar hunts fatigue. That is the whole distinction and it comes straight out of Dougou's own canonical doctrine: do not break the wall, make the wall confess where it was already tired.

title: Percussion uses plate rather than defeating it; the tell
summary: Percussion does not seek to penetrate plate, it uses it — armour transmits force inward, so the target is the joint, base and balance, making the plate expensive to wear. The tell is that the fighter tracks breathing and footing rather than the weapon.
verbatim: Percussion answers to plate: none of these seek to penetrate. Plate is not defeated by percussion, it is used. The armour transmits force inward, and the correct target is the joint, the base, the balance and the man's ability to keep standing in fifty pounds of steel. A percussion fighter's answer to plate is to make the plate expensive to wear.
