title: One sustained elegiac passage per scene at most
summary: At most one sustained elegiac passage per scene, which may sit anywhere except the closing beat, which still ends on physical action per Scene Standards.
verbatim: Budget: one sustained elegiac passage per scene at most, and it may sit anywhere except the closing beat, which per Scene Standards still ends on physical action.
notes: Elevated to status:live: Pack Fifteen §4 (already ratified, live) explicitly confirms this instrument "stands," following the same precedent used for Pack Seven content Pack Twelve confirms survives.

title: Per-culture narration registers, extended from dialogue
summary: Free indirect discourse's per-character register licence is raised to a per-culture one: proposed narration registers include Dawi (stressed monosyllables, concrete nouns, sentence-level distrust of abstraction), Eresse (subordination, latinate diction, periodic sentences), Concord human (the house baseline), and Moto (to be built, highest-priority gap).
verbatim: The extension raises it from a per-character instruction to a per-culture one. Proposed narration registers, to be built out per culture as POVs arrive: - Dawi POV. Stressed monosyllables, short clauses, concrete nouns, tools named by their proper names. Abstractions distrusted at sentence level as well as in dialogue. - Eresse POV. Subordination, latinate diction, periodic sentences that withhold the verb. Time referenced in long units. - Concord human POV. The house baseline. Everything else is measured against it. - Moto POV. To be built. Flagged as the highest-priority gap since it carries the current arc.
ratified: Isaac, 2026-09-12, Claude Code ruling session: Pack Five's remaining proposed rows ratified
notes: This is the "register by culture" rule Pack Fifteen §1 strikes down to flavour ("Available as flavour. Not law."): see R15-1-REGISTER_BY_CULTURE, which should be backfilled to reference this row by id (a demotion since flavour use remains available, so no supersedes link — same policy as other demotions in this corpus).

title: The funeral test for a joke
summary: Could this line be said at a funeral, by someone who means it, without breaking the room? If the humour needs a comedic frame to work, cut it.
verbatim: The test: could this line be said at a funeral, by someone who means it, without breaking the room? If the humour requires a comedic frame to work, cut it.
notes: Elevated to status:live: Pack Fifteen §4 (already ratified, live) explicitly confirms this instrument "stands," following the same precedent used for Pack Seven content Pack Twelve confirms survives.

title: Humour never gets its own setup/deadpan/reaction rhythm
summary: The beat structure of setup, deadpan and reaction is barred; humour arrives inside dialogue and narration already in progress and never pauses the scene to land.
verbatim: Barred: the beat structure of setup, deadpan and reaction. Humour no longer gets its own rhythm. It arrives inside dialogue and narration already in progress and does not pause the scene to land.
notes: Elevated to status:live: Pack Fifteen §4 (already ratified, live) explicitly confirms this instrument "stands," following the same precedent used for Pack Seven content Pack Twelve confirms survives.

title: Who currently carries humour, and who does not
summary: Lambert carries institutional dryness in the debrief; Pietro carries contempt as wit; Yoko is accidentally funny through literalism; Sodoku does not make jokes and should not start.
verbatim: Who carries it, current cast: Lambert (institutional dryness, arrives in the debrief). Pietro (contempt as wit). Yoko (accidental, through literalism). Sodoku does not make jokes and should not start.
notes: Elevated to status:live: Pack Fifteen §4 (already ratified, live) explicitly confirms this instrument "stands," following the same precedent used for Pack Seven content Pack Twelve confirms survives.

title: Humour is a character property, not a tone exception
summary: Humour is no longer an exception to tone but a property of specific characters in the Abercrombie register: dry understatement, gallows wit from those whose profession earns it, class-inflected contempt, a character being funny without knowing it, and the joke that is also a threat.
verbatim: Permitted: dry understatement, gallows wit from people whose profession earns it, class-inflected contempt, a character being funny without knowing it, and the joke that is also a threat.
notes: Elevated to status:live: Pack Fifteen §4 (already ratified, live) explicitly confirms this instrument "stands," following the same precedent used for Pack Seven content Pack Twelve confirms survives.

title: The elegiac register is allowed in scene narration
summary: The elegiac register is available to scene narration because elegy in the saga mode reports a loss rather than judging it; Section C.2's flat-delivery rule is what keeps it on the correct side of the line.
verbatim: The elegiac register is available to scene narration, because elegy in the saga mode reports a loss rather than judging it. Section C.2's flat-delivery rule is what keeps it on the correct side of this line.
notes: Elevated to status:live: Pack Fifteen §4 (already ratified, live) explicitly confirms this instrument "stands," following the same precedent used for Pack Seven content Pack Twelve confirms survives.

title: The elevated register is quarantined to documents and myth
summary: The elevated register (invocation, myth-cadence, high style) is available only to in-world documents, songs, oral-tradition passages, mythic strata, prophetic/Celestial Host material, and the opening/closing frame of a mythic-scale event — not ordinary scene narration.
verbatim: The elevated register, meaning invocation, myth-cadence and the high style, is available to in-world documents, songs, oral-tradition passages, the mythic strata, prophetic and Celestial Host material, and the opening or closing frame of a mythic-scale event. Not to ordinary scene narration.
notes: Elevated to status:live: Pack Fifteen §4 (already ratified, live) explicitly confirms this instrument "stands," following the same precedent used for Pack Seven content Pack Twelve confirms survives.

title: Free indirect discourse remains the carve-out
summary: A moral verdict in the POV's own idiom, which could be wrong, is characterisation; the same verdict in the narrator's neutral register is Tolkien's voice and gets cut, per Pack Four's gloss test.
verbatim: Free indirect discourse remains the carve-out and Pack Four's gloss test still governs. A moral verdict in the POV's own idiom, which could be wrong, is characterisation. The same verdict in the narrator's neutral register is Tolkien's voice and gets cut.
notes: Elevated to status:live: Pack Fifteen §4 (already ratified, live) explicitly confirms this instrument "stands," following the same precedent used for Pack Seven content Pack Twelve confirms survives.

title: Martin wins on narration authority
summary: Martin wins on narration authority: Tolkien's elevated and elegiac register is available, his moral voice is not.
verbatim: Ruling proposed: Martin wins on narration authority. Tolkien's elevated and elegiac register is available, his moral voice is not.
notes: This exact proposal is Section H's pending ruling #1 (R5-H-NARRATION_AUTHORITY_PENDING); kept here as the concrete proposed rule and separately as the open ruling, matching how other packs record a proposed answer alongside its own pending status.

title: Third-person narration is POV-locked and never adjudicates
summary: Third-person scene narration is POV-locked and never adjudicates; no line tells the reader what to think of a character's choice.
verbatim: Third-person scene narration is POV-locked and never adjudicates. No line tells the reader what to think of a character's choice.
notes: Elevated to status:live: Pack Fifteen §4 (already ratified, live) explicitly confirms this instrument "stands," following the same precedent used for Pack Seven content Pack Twelve confirms survives.

title: What the light novel keeps
summary: The chapter as a hard unit with one objective and a hook at close; legibility as reader pleasure (the argument for the Codex); and fast entry, chapters opening inside the situation.
verbatim: The chapter as a hard unit with one clear objective and a hook at close. Serialised discipline, directly relevant to The Withering Road. - Legibility as reader pleasure. The satisfaction of a system the reader can reason inside. This is the whole argument for the Codex and it survives the register change intact. - Fast entry. Chapters open inside the situation.
ratified: Isaac, 2026-09-12, Claude Code ruling session: Pack Five's remaining proposed rows ratified

title: What the light novel does not keep
summary: Status screens, panels and HUD-style rendering (already banned); narrator explanation of the system to the reader; the isekai commentary register (wry narrator asides about the world's rules); and character-sheet vocabulary (Stage, Grade, eta, Band) surfacing in prose.
verbatim: - Status screens, panels, HUD-style rendering. Already banned; restated because the light-novel framing invites them back. - Narrator explanation of the system to the reader. Section 3.1's Mechanism Standard delivers mechanism through physical description at trigger points, never as instruction. - The isekai commentary register. Wry narrator asides about the world's rules. - Character-sheet vocabulary surfacing in prose. Stage, Grade, eta and Band are author-facing.
ratified: Isaac, 2026-09-12, Claude Code ruling session: Pack Five's remaining proposed rows ratified

title: The Manhwa Energy Directive is struck from project instructions
summary: The Manhwa Energy Directive block is struck in full from project instructions, "manhwa-cinematic" and "manhwa energy" are struck from tone descriptions, and the genre-intersection statement is amended so only the pacing ambition survives.
verbatim: - Strike the Manhwa Energy Directive block in full. - Strike "manhwa-cinematic" and "manhwa energy" from tone descriptions. - Amend the genre-intersection statement: the pacing ambition survives, the manhwa-cinematic layer does not.

title: Manhwa Energy Directive added to the deliberately-excluded list
summary: The Master Style Directive's §10 deliberately-excluded list gains the Manhwa Energy Directive.
verbatim: Sec. 10: add the Manhwa Energy Directive to the deliberately-excluded list.

title: Directive §4's manhwa-humour clause replaced with a pointer to D
summary: The Master Style Directive's §4 final paragraph (the manhwa-energy humour clause) is deleted and replaced with a pointer to Pack Five Section D.
verbatim: Sec. 4, final paragraph: delete the manhwa-energy-humour clause entirely. Replace with a pointer to Pack Five Sec. D.

title: Four new active tells added
summary: Declarative characterisation and the reaction-shot cutaway (from Section B's confirmed repeal) plus the comedic beat structure and narrator moral adjudication (from Sections D and E, still proposed) are added as active tells.
verbatim: Add as active tells: declarative characterisation, the reaction-shot cutaway, the comedic beat structure, narrator moral adjudication.
ratified: Isaac, 2026-09-12, Claude Code ruling session: Pack Five's remaining proposed rows ratified
notes: Kept at status:proposed as a whole even though two of its four tells (declarative characterisation, reaction-shot cutaway) trace to the confirmed Section B repeal, since the other two trace to still-proposed Sections D and E; a conservative bundling rather than splitting into four rows.

title: Build per-culture narration registers now or defer
summary: Whether per-culture narration registers (Section C.3) are built out now or deferred until a POV in each culture exists; the Moto register is needed either way for the current arc.
verbatim: Per-culture narration registers (Sec. C.3): build out now, or defer until a POV in each culture actually exists? Moto register is needed either way for the current arc.
ratified: Isaac, 2026-09-12, Claude Code: defer until a POV in that culture exists
notes: RULED 2026-09-12: defer. Build a culture's narration register when a POV in that culture actually exists, not ahead of need. The Moto register is already built (needed for the current arc).

title: Does the elegiac mode become standing craft law
summary: Whether the elegiac mode (Section C.2) is installed as standing craft law; it would permanently change the Withering's emotional shape.
verbatim: Does the elegiac mode get installed as standing craft law (Sec. C.2)? It changes the emotional shape of the Withering permanently.
ratified: Isaac, 2026-09-12, Claude Code: yes, install it as standing law
notes: RULED 2026-09-12: yes, standing craft law (already live in practice via Pack Fifteen §4 and the R5-C2-* rows; this closes the formal docket entry on the same basis).

title: Does Martin win on narration authority
summary: Whether Martin wins on narration authority (Section E); the proposed answer is yes, with the elevated register quarantined to documents and mythic strata — the load-bearing call in the pack.
verbatim: Does Martin win on narration authority (Sec. E)? The proposed answer is yes, with the elevated register quarantined to in-world documents and mythic strata. This is the load-bearing call in the pack.
ratified: Isaac, 2026-09-12, Claude Code: judged per scene by what the scene needs, not a fixed quarantine
notes: RULED 2026-09-12: Martin wins (already live via Pack Fifteen §4 and R5-E-MARTIN_WINS_RULING). The proposed fixed quarantine (elevated register only in documents and mythic strata) is replaced: whether a given scene gets the elevated register is a per-scene call based on what that scene needs, not a structural rule tied to document type.

title: Does the Kharven arc get a retroactive register pass
summary: Whether the eight Kharven prose scenes, written under the manhwa directive, are left forward-only or the arc gets a register pass.
verbatim: Retroactive application. The eight Kharven prose scenes were written under the manhwa directive. Forward-only, or does the arc get a register pass?
ratified: Isaac, 2026-09-12, Claude Code: forward-only, no rewrite pass
notes: RULED 2026-09-12: forward-only. The eight existing Kharven scenes stand as written; only new Kharven prose follows the current register. No retroactive pass on the arc.

title: The Ladder — two abstraction-chain clauses is an automatic cut
summary: Two or more clauses of the form "X was Y and Y was Z" in one sentence is an automatic cut, never a rewrite; cut back to the first concrete noun. Restating a concrete observation as an abstraction in the following sentence is barred the same way.
verbatim: The rule. Two or more clauses of the form X was Y and Y was Z in the same sentence is an automatic cut, never a rewrite. Cut back to the first concrete noun and stop there.
notes: Explicitly reaffirmed by Pack Twelve §7: "Retained in full: the Ladder ban... Explaining a mechanism is no licence to write badly." (R12-7-AI_TELLS_RETAINED).

title: The Inventory is where elegiac things live
summary: Pack Five's elegiac register requires a named concrete thing that is gone, and the Inventory is where those things live; elegy without an Inventory is grief for abstractions, which Pack Five already bars.
verbatim: Pack Five's elegiac register (Sec. C.2) requires a named concrete thing that is gone. The Inventory is where those things live. A dye colour no longer made, a dish nobody can assemble since the corridor closed, a proverb whose second half has been lost.

title: Check 18 — the Ladder
summary: Flags any sentence containing two or more instances of the "was X and the X was" pattern, including is/became/meant variants.
verbatim: Check 18, the Ladder. Flag any sentence containing two or more instances of was [a-z]+ and the [a-z]+ was. Also flag the variants using is, became, and meant.

title: Check 19 — apparatus subject
summary: Flags any sentence where a named faculty is the grammatical subject of a perception verb; high false-positive rate by design, reviewed by reading.
verbatim: Check 19, apparatus subject. Flag any sentence where a named faculty is the grammatical subject of a perception verb. High false-positive rate by design; review by reading.
notes: Pack Fourteen §6 later says "Check 19 rewritten off §4" (Twelve's four explaining voices); see R12-8-VERIFY_CHECKS_RETIRED, which names checks 20/21 retired and check 19 rewritten rather than retired — this row is not marked superseded since it's rewritten, not struck, and no replacement check text is given anywhere in this corpus to point to instead.

title: Four surviving Tell Bank additions
summary: Added to the AI tells checklist and retained in full per Pack Twelve §7 — the Ladder in all forms, the apparatus as grammatical subject, scientific vocabulary explaining an ambient sensory impression, and fresh texture invented where Inventory texture exists.
verbatim: The Ladder in all forms. - The apparatus as grammatical subject. - Scientific vocabulary explaining an ambient sensory impression.
notes: Kept live per R12-7-AI_TELLS_RETAINED ("Retained in full... every AI tell in the checklist").

title: The total-legibility tell is struck
summary: The tell for total legibility — a scene in which every perception is understood at the moment of perception — is struck.
verbatim: Total legibility: a scene in which every perception is understood at the moment of perception.
notes: Superseded by R12-7-LEGIBILITY_BAN_STRUCK.

title: Is the Inventory a Notion wiki or a markdown guide
summary: Whether the Standing Inventory is a Notion wiki section or a standing markdown guide.
verbatim: Whether the Inventory is a Notion wiki section or a standing markdown guide. Proposed: Notion, one page per culture under a new Standing Inventory section page, since it will be queried mid-scene.
notes: DECIDED IN PRACTICE, 2026-09-12, against this row's own proposal: all six built as standing markdown guides (desktop/inventories/*.md), not Notion pages. The WOTR MCP's session_start/scene_brief already read from that folder (`_inventory`), so this is load-bearing, not a placeholder choice -- reopening it would mean migrating six live files into Notion for no functional gain.

title: Standing Inventory build order
summary: What order the remaining cultures' Standing Inventories are built in.
verbatim: Inventory build order. Kharven and the Moto are drafted. Proposed sequence after: Stannvaard, the Dawi, Ketsuen, Nalūn, the Yukari enclave.

title: Is the one-read-per-scene ceiling correct
summary: Whether the one-read-per-scene ceiling is correct, or a scholar POV in active diagnosis should get more.
verbatim: The one-read-per-scene ceiling. Correct number, or should a scholar POV in active diagnosis get more?
notes: Moot: R12-7-APPARATUS_CAP_REPLACED strikes the one-read-per-scene cap in quotable words; a faculty may read as often as the scene needs, at a tempo cost. Closed 2026-09-12.

title: Does a Ladder pass run across the archive
summary: Whether the Ladder rule applies forward-only or a Ladder pass runs across the whole archive, given Check 18 finds instances cheaply.
verbatim: Retroactive application. The Cozbi cycle and the enclave scene are the worst offenders in the corpus. Forward-only, or does a Ladder pass get run across the archive?
ratified: Isaac, 2026-09-12, Claude Code: forward-only
notes: RULED 2026-09-12: forward-only. No retroactive Ladder pass across the archive; the Cozbi cycle and the enclave scene stand as written.

title: The chemistry ban corollary
summary: Real-world scientific vocabulary explaining a sensory impression is barred unless the POV is a practitioner of that specific craft actively diagnosing; the Mechanism Standard governs technique trigger points and nothing else, never a licence for ambient exposition.
verbatim: Corollary, the chemistry ban. Real-world scientific vocabulary explaining a sensory impression is out unless the POV is a practitioner of that specific craft actively diagnosing. Calcium oxide releasing its held breath is the narrator being a chemist in a scene about a burned village.
notes: Explicitly confirmed surviving by Pack Thirteen §6 (R13-6-CHEMISTRY_BAN_SCOPE): "Pack Six's chemistry ban survives for ambient sensory impression. It does not touch a hit, a wound, or a working."

title: The faculty is never the grammatical subject
summary: A named faculty is never the grammatical subject of a perception verb; the character perceives, the apparatus does not act on its own behalf.
verbatim: The faculty is never the grammatical subject. Barred: his Cymorath mapped the thinning. Permitted: the fourth layer had thinned. The character perceives. The apparatus does not act on its own behalf.
notes: Only the one-read-per-scene frequency cap is struck by Pack Twelve §7; this grammatical-subject rule is never named as struck and is part of the "every AI tell in the checklist" retained in full.

title: One reading per scene cap
summary: A perceptive faculty may deliver a single explicit read per scene; after that it is silent and the character perceives with a body.
verbatim: One reading per scene. A perceptive faculty may deliver a single explicit read. After that it is silent and the character perceives with a body: eyes, nose, skin, memory, guesswork.
notes: Superseded by R12-7-APPARATUS_CAP_REPLACED ("Struck: the Apparatus Rule's one-read-per-scene cap... Replaced by a cost").

title: The read delivers a fact, never an interpretation
summary: A faculty's read delivers a bare fact ("Twenty-three"), never an interpretation woven around it; the faculty is an instrument and instruments produce numbers, not meaning.
verbatim: The read delivers a fact, never an interpretation. Twenty-three. Not twenty-three, and the Cymorath filed the count with the flat unasked-for fidelity it filed everything. The faculty is an instrument, and instruments produce numbers, not meaning.

title: The ignorance quota, minimum one per scene
summary: At least one thing per scene the POV notices and cannot interpret; the narration does not rescue him, and resolution comes in a later scene or chapter.
verbatim: Minimum one per scene, mandatory. The POV notices something and cannot interpret it. The narration does not rescue him. Resolution comes in a later scene, and preferably a later chapter.
notes: Explicitly reaffirmed and elevated by Pack Twelve §7 (R12-7-IGNORANCE_MISREADING_RETAINED): "now more important... the wrong explanation is the load-bearing device."

title: The misreading budget, at least one wrong inference per scene
summary: At least one POV inference per scene is wrong and is not corrected on the page; the misreading must be reasonable, consistent with what the POV knows, and left standing for the reader to find later.
verbatim: At least one POV inference per scene is wrong, and is not corrected on the page. Competent characters reaching wrong conclusions from good reasoning is the whole Ned Stark instrument. A character who is never wrong is a camera. The misreading must be reasonable, must be consistent with what that POV knows, and must be left standing so the reader can find it later.
notes: Explicitly reaffirmed and elevated by Pack Twelve §7 (R12-7-IGNORANCE_MISREADING_RETAINED).

title: "Interpret it at zero" is struck
summary: The blanket rule that objects, weather, injury, wear and labour are rendered exhaustively but never interpreted is struck.
verbatim: The distinction: describe the world at full density, interpret it at zero. Objects, weather, injury, wear, labour, all rendered exhaustively. Meaning, significance, thematic weight, all withheld.
notes: Superseded by R12-7-LEGIBILITY_BAN_STRUCK ("Struck: the total-legibility ban and the blanket interpretation-at-zero rule.").

title: Material density stays; described at full density, interpreted at zero
summary: Material density (rust, weathering, wear, labour) stays described in full per the Directive; the distinction is that the world is described exhaustively but interpreted at zero — meaning and thematic weight are withheld.
verbatim: The material density stays. Seven of thirty-two structures burned. Hanuri re-spinning thread from an older garment. Bedding planes in limestone. The rust described in full remains house law (Directive Sec. 1.2) and Pack Six removes nothing from it.

title: Texture from the Standing Inventory, mechanism from the Codex
summary: Texture comes from the Standing Inventory; mechanism comes from the Codex; a scene that reaches for the Codex when it needs texture has failed.
verbatim: Texture comes from the Standing Inventory. Mechanism comes from the Codex. A scene that reaches for the Codex when it needs texture has failed.

title: The Standing Inventory's nine required categories
summary: Food, the greeting, oaths and obscenity, colloquial time, the dead, the household object, exchange, proverbs, and the body — each entry must be causally downstream of the culture's material conditions; flavour-only invention is rejected.
verbatim: A per-culture register of non-magical material idiom, built and maintained as canon. Nine required categories:

title: Identity is repetition; every scene draws from the Inventory first
summary: Every scene draws texture from the Inventory before inventing anything; anything newly invented is entered into the Inventory the same session or it does not exist; each culture designates three-to-five high-frequency signature items on the Recurrence Ledger.
verbatim: Identity is repetition. Novelty is its enemy.

title: Character first, system second
summary: Refusal, wound and conviction produce the phenomenon; the Codex files it afterward and is not a generator.
verbatim: Character first, system second. Refusal, wound and conviction produce the phenomenon. The Codex files it afterward. The Codex is not a generator.
notes: Explicitly reaffirmed by R12-8-ABILITY_GUIDE_REWRITE: "Character-first design order survives untouched and is unaffected by this pack."

title: Hard world, soft magic — never the mechanism
summary: The world obeys itself absolutely and nobody explains why; a reader needs the cost, the limit and the rough weight, never the mechanism.
verbatim: Hard world, soft magic. The world obeys itself absolutely and nobody explains why. A reader needs the cost, the limit, and the rough weight. Never the mechanism.
notes: Superseded by R12-1-MECHANISM_NOWHERE_STRUCK / R12-1-EXPLAIN_BAN_STRUCK.

title: The three hard rails — economy, ladder, lineage
summary: Three things never bend: the economy (finite, spent, visible), the ladder (sixteen Stages, felt before seen), and the lineage (everything traceable to a source).
verbatim: The three hard rails, which never bend: the economy (finite, spent, visible), the ladder (sixteen Stages, felt before seen), the lineage (everything came from somewhere traceable).
notes: The economy and the ladder are explicitly reaffirmed by R12-1-PACK_SEVEN_SURVIVORS ("The economy is still a hard rail... The ladder is still real"); the lineage clause isn't separately named there but is never struck either, so the whole row is kept live rather than split.

title: The three soft zones — mechanism, catalogue, origin
summary: Mechanism, catalogue and origin are the three things never explained.
verbatim: The three soft zones, never explained: mechanism, catalogue, origin.
notes: Superseded by R12-1-SOFT_ZONES_STRUCK ("the three soft zones as a blanket rule... Struck, with one flagged exception at §6").

title: Two ledgers — the page and the workbook
summary: The page gets Effect, Cost, Limit, Counter, and one line of what nobody knows; the workbook keeps every other field and is never published.
verbatim: Two ledgers. The page gets Effect, Cost, Limit, Counter, and one line of what nobody knows. The workbook keeps every other field and is never published.
notes: Superseded by R12-8-ABILITY_GUIDE_REWRITE: "The two-ledger split is retired; there is now one ledger with a summary card."

title: A character explaining their own Design Chain is cut on sight
summary: A character explaining the Trigger, Mechanism and Counterplay of their own technique is character-sheet vocabulary in dialogue and is cut on sight.
verbatim: Added: the same restriction now covers the Design Chain by name. A character explaining the Trigger, Mechanism and Counterplay of their own technique is character-sheet vocabulary in dialogue and is cut on sight.
notes: Superseded by Pack Twelve's four explaining voices, which explicitly license this kind of dialogue (R12-4-VOICE_ONE_POV, R12-4-VOICE_THREE_OPPONENT).

title: The Design Chain is filled and consulted, never published
summary: The ten-field Design Chain (Trigger, Function, Mechanism, Numerical Effect, Target Response, Consequence, Limitation, Weakness, Cost, Counterplay) is a design instrument, filled before writing, consulted while writing, published never.
verbatim: Renamed: the Design Chain. Filled before writing, consulted while writing, published never.
notes: Superseded by R12-1-DESIGN_CHAIN_RETURNS / R12-3-DESIGN_CHAIN_RETURNS ("Now prose-legal in full"); the ten-field list itself is what Pack Twelve §3 restores, so the chain's contents carry forward even though this row's "published never" rule is dead.

title: An inexplicable rescue is licensed if its cost is reasoned
summary: A character may be rescued by something the reader cannot explain, provided the reader can reason about what it cost.
verbatim: The line that replaces the rest: a character may be rescued by something the reader cannot explain, provided the reader can reason about what it cost.
notes: Superseded along with the rest of the pack by R12-1-PACK_SEVEN_REPEALED; no specific Pack Twelve line addresses this particular clause.

title: Titans, Archons and Epoch-scale events generate dread, never resolve
summary: The Titans, the Archons, the Crevice, the Withering and anything Epoch-scale generate problems, dread and awe; they never resolve a plot.
verbatim: The surviving line, unchanged and still load-bearing: the Titans, the Archons, the Crevice, the Withering and anything Epoch-scale generate problems, dread and awe. They never resolve a plot.
notes: Restated almost verbatim in Pack Twelve's R12-A ("They generate dread and problems. They never resolve a plot."), which pitches keeping Origin mythic; kept live since nothing ever struck it.

title: Mechanism/counterplay/training explanation dropped as number triggers
summary: Mechanism reveal, counterplay explanation and training explanation are struck from the trigger list for numbers on the page — workbook events only.
verbatim: Struck from the trigger list: mechanism reveal, counterplay explanation, training explanation. Those are workbook events and no longer occasions for numbers on the page.
notes: Superseded by R12-1-EXPLAIN_BAN_STRUCK / R12-1-NUMBER_BAN_STRUCK.

title: Exact numbers still belong at four occasions
summary: Exact numbers still belong at a character-sheet breakdown, a major injury, an armour or structural failure, and a high-stakes finisher.
verbatim: Mostly survives. Exact numbers still belong at a character-sheet breakdown, a major injury, an armour or structural failure, and a high-stakes finisher.
notes: Superseded along with the rest of the pack; Pack Fourteen's stat display rules (R14-4-EFFECTS_CHANNEL, R14-4-DIAGNOSTIC_CHANNEL) now govern this territory instead.

title: Hard by kind — cost, limit, weight and the numbered facts
summary: Hard, never bending: cost, limit, relative weight, cause and consequence, the sixteen Stages, the eight Families, the sixty Wellsprings, the Codex grammar, and relative strength. Soft, never explained: how any of it works, how much exists, and where it came from.
verbatim: Hard, and it never bends: cost, limit, relative weight, cause and consequence, the sixteen Stages, the eight Families, the sixty Wellsprings, the Codex grammar, and who is stronger than whom. Soft, and never explained: how any of it works, how much of it exists, and where it came from.
notes: The "how any of it works" clause is superseded by Pack Twelve's general mechanism-explanation repeal; "where it came from" (Origin) surviving as mythic is exactly what Pack Twelve's own R12-A pitches as a recommendation, so that half continues in spirit even though this specific row is marked dead along with the rest of the pack.

title: Numbers attach to physical reality only
summary: A metre, a temperature, a mass, a duration take a unit; nothing metaphysical ever does.
verbatim: The corollary stands and is strengthened. Numbers attach to physical reality only. A metre, a temperature, a mass, a duration. Nothing metaphysical takes a unit, ever.
notes: Superseded by R12-1-NUMBER_BAN_STRUCK and rationed rather than banned by R12-5-NUMBERS_DIAGNOSTIC_ONLY.

title: Existing techniques get retroactive Design Chains, no page changes
summary: Existing named techniques get retroactive Design Chains in the workbook only, with no page changes, since the old page standard no longer applies to prose.
verbatim: Answer: they get retroactive Design Chains in the workbook, and no page changes at all. The standard they were being held to no longer applies to prose, so there is nothing to retrofit into the archive.
notes: Superseded along with the workbook-only Design Chain rule it depends on.

title: Trigger points get physical disclosure, not mechanism disclosure
summary: A first display, a major injury and a Domain activation no longer trigger a mechanism disclosure; they trigger a physical disclosure only.
verbatim: What is repealed is the instruction to put it on the page at trigger points. A first display, a major injury and a Domain activation no longer trigger a mechanism disclosure. They trigger a physical disclosure.
notes: Superseded by R12-1-EXPLAIN_BAN_STRUCK and R12-3-COMBAT_EXCHANGE_OWES, which restore mechanism/counter disclosure at these same trigger points.

title: The physical-disclosure standard at trigger points
summary: At a trigger point, the page gets what the body did, what the room did, what the target felt, and what it cost, visibly — the mechanism stays in the workbook.
verbatim: What replaces it at trigger points. At a first display, a major injury, a Domain activation or a finisher, the page gets: - What the body did. - What the air, the ground and the objects in the room did. - What the target felt, in the target's own physical terms. - What it cost, visibly.
notes: Superseded in substance by R12-3-COMBAT_EXCHANGE_OWES and later expanded by R13-4-COMBAT_FLOOR's eight-item version.

title: Pressure — a stronger practitioner is felt before anything is cast
summary: Presence precedes technique: one Stage up bends the room's attention; two causes physical distress; three or more causes involuntary submission; a Band gap changes local weather and animal behaviour. Felt in the body, never described as an aura from outside; the POV misreads it at least once.
verbatim: Presence precedes technique. A stronger practitioner is felt in a room, physically and involuntarily, before anything is cast.
notes: Marked superseded per the wholesale repeal of Pack Seven, though "Pressure" as a concept is used freely and without caveat by every later pack (Nine, Eleven, Fourteen) as settled worldbuilding — those later packs stand on their own textual authority, not on this row remaining live.

title: A duel is an information problem before a physical one
summary: Taught techniques are counterable by anyone who studied the same material; self-derived techniques must be read live under pressure, with at least one wrong conclusion per the misreading budget.
verbatim: A duel between competent practitioners is an information problem before it is a physical one. The winner is usually whoever identifies what the other is doing first.
notes: Marked superseded along with the rest of the pack, though its core idea (documented vs. self-derived techniques, read live) is carried forward almost exactly by R12-3-NAMED_INVENTOR_RULE.

title: The three-layer hit model, rendered as phenomena not explanation
summary: Physics, Essence and Hermetic correspondence — two visible per meaningful hit, all three at a first display or finisher — rendered as phenomena (what the air did), never as explanations (why).
verbatim: The three-layer hit model survives intact. Physics, Essence and Hermetic correspondence, two visible per meaningful hit, all three at a first display or a finisher. Clarified: the Essence and Hermetic layers are rendered as phenomena, never as explanations. What the air did, not why it did it.
notes: The three-layer structure itself continues (Pack Thirteen §4's three explanations use the same physics/Essence/Hermetic triad), but "never as explanations" is exactly reversed by R13-4-THREE_EXPLANATIONS; marked superseded along with the rest of the pack, no specific Pack Twelve line names this clause directly.

title: Combat trigger points hit the physical standard, not mechanism
summary: A technique's first display, major injury or finisher hits the physical standard (real units on the body, armour and ground); the metaphysical half of the old chain moves to the workbook.
verbatim: Struck: a technique's first display, a major injury or a finisher hits the Scientific Mechanism Standard. Replaced: a technique's first display, a major injury or a finisher hits the physical standard. Real units on the body, the armour and the ground. The metaphysical half of the old chain moves to the workbook.
notes: Superseded by R12-8-COMBAT_GUIDE_READ_LENGTH and Pack Thirteen's combat technical floor.

title: The inscription Function field is physical terms only
summary: The inscription Function field states physical terms only; the system term goes in the workbook line, not the field itself.
verbatim: The inscription Function field says physical terms first, system terms second. Amended: physical terms only. The system term goes in the workbook line.
notes: Superseded by Pack Twelve/Thirteen's diagnostic-voice system terms (system terms may now appear alongside their dramatisation, per R13-9-STYLE_DIRECTIVE_MECHANISM_VOCAB).

title: The Dragonslayer, not Shardblades, is the hard-magic-object lesson
summary: The tertiary-source note's Shardblades citation is replaced: what Miura does with the Dragonslayer (an object that became a geological feature through accumulated use) is the lesson — an object's rules matter less than its history.
verbatim: Replaced: what Miura does with the Dragonslayer, an object that became a geological feature through accumulated use, is the lesson. An object's rules matter less than its history.
notes: Superseded along with the rest of the pack by R12-1-PACK_SEVEN_REPEALED; no specific Item Guide successor is named elsewhere in the corpus so far.

title: The Design Chain is suspended in the Close Register
summary: The Design Chain is suspended in the Close Register, requiring an analytical observer, available in a pre-engagement scene, a commander's briefing, or the aftermath.
verbatim: The suspension line survives with the rename. The Design Chain is suspended in the Close Register. It requires an analytical observer, and it remains available in a pre-engagement scene, a commander's briefing, or the aftermath.
notes: Superseded along with the workbook-only Design Chain rule it depends on.

title: Pressure is legible in the press when nothing else is
summary: A practitioner's pressure is legible in a mass-combat press because it arrives through the body rather than the eye; a line that breaks before contact broke because of something it felt.
verbatim: Added: Pressure is the exception. A practitioner's pressure is legible in the press when nothing else is, because it arrives through the body rather than the eye. A line that breaks before contact broke because of something it felt.

title: Pack Five's narrator-explanation bar becomes absolute
summary: Pack Five's bar on narrator explanation of the system now agrees with the base guides; the Section 3.1 delivery route it cited is closed, and the bar is absolute.
verbatim: Pack Five's bar on narrator explanation of the system to the reader now agrees with the base guides instead of contradicting them. It cited Section 3.1 as the permitted delivery route; that route is closed and the bar is absolute.
notes: Superseded along with the rest of the pack; Section 3.1's route is reopened by R12-1-EXPLAIN_BAN_STRUCK, so Pack Five's original bar (if it survives Pack Five's own extraction) may be live again — confirm in Phase 2 when Pack Five is extracted.

title: Pack Six's chemistry ban and Apparatus Rule are strengthened
summary: Pack Six's chemistry ban and Apparatus Rule are unchanged and strengthened; Pack Six restricted the Mechanism Standard to technique trigger points, and Pack Seven removes the trigger points as well.
verbatim: Pack Six's chemistry ban and Apparatus Rule are unchanged and strengthened. Pack Six restricted the Mechanism Standard to technique trigger points. Pack Seven removes the trigger points as well.
notes: Superseded along with the trigger points it removes; Pack Six's chemistry ban itself is untouched (see R13-6-CHEMISTRY_BAN_SCOPE).

title: New pre-write question, POV understanding vs. observation
summary: Before writing any scene containing a working, state what the POV understands about what just happened versus what they merely observe; the gap is written and left open.
verbatim: New pre-write question, added to the canon check. Before writing any scene containing a working: what does the POV understand about what just happened, and what do they merely observe? The gap is written and left open.
notes: Superseded by R12-8-SCENE_GUIDE_PACK7_STRUCK ("The Pack Seven pre-write question and self-review check are struck.") — a clean named match.

title: New self-review check, no line explains why a working worked
summary: No line in a scene explains why a working worked.
verbatim: New self-review check. No line in the scene explains why a working worked.
notes: Superseded by R12-8-SCENE_GUIDE_PACK7_STRUCK — the same clean named match as R7-4-PREWRITE_QUESTION.

title: The character-first re-derivation pass
summary: For each major character, state what they refuse, what they survived, and what they believe that costs them, then check the phenomenon actually comes out of it; where it does not, the ability needs rebuilding from the person, not the Physics Domain.
verbatim: The character-first re-derivation. For each major character, state what they refuse, what they survived, and what they believe that costs them, then check the phenomenon actually comes out of it. Where it does not, the ability was generated from a Physics Domain and needs rebuilding from the person.
notes: Kept live alongside R7-1-CHARACTER_FIRST, which R12-8-ABILITY_GUIDE_REWRITE explicitly says survives untouched.

title: The cost audit, largest job on the docket
summary: An estimated sixty percent of existing technique entries fail the test that "overuse strains him" is not a real cost; every failure needs a real cost category, something the character still carries when nobody is fighting.
verbatim: The cost audit. Working estimate is that sixty percent of existing technique entries fail the test that overuse-strains-him is not a cost. Every failure needs a real category from the wheel: something the character still carries when nobody is fighting. This is the largest and most valuable job on the docket.
notes: Kept live: Pack Seventeen §9 still treats "Pack Seven's cost audit" as the largest open job on the docket, not something the Pack Twelve repeal touched — the audit is a production process, not a prose restriction.

title: The naming pass against the one-beat test
summary: Every existing technique name is checked against the one-beat test; failures are flagged but nothing is renamed without Isaac's ruling.
verbatim: The naming pass. Every existing technique name against the one-beat test. Flag failures, do not rename anything without Isaac's ruling, since some of these are established in prose.
notes: Superseded along with the rest of the pack; Pack Eight's naming pass (R8-27-STANDING_TASK) is a different mechanic (true names/registers, not the one-beat test) and doesn't replace this specifically.

title: Check 20 — the mechanism gloss
summary: Flags any sentence in prose that explains why a working produced its effect; physical description passes, causal explanation fails.
verbatim: Check 20, the mechanism gloss. Any sentence in prose that explains why a working produced its effect. Detection is imperfect and manual review is required. The physical description of what happened is not a hit. The causal account of why is.
notes: Superseded by R12-1-EXPLAIN_BAN_STRUCK and retired outright by R12-8-VERIFY_CHECKS_RETIRED... actually retired checks there are 20 and 21, matching exactly.

title: Check 21 — metaphysical units
summary: Flags any number attached to a non-physical quantity; physical units (metres, degrees, kilograms, seconds, distances) pass, Essence/ Coherence/resonance/Wellspring-output figures fail.
verbatim: Check 21, metaphysical units. Any number attached to a non-physical quantity. Metres, degrees, kilograms, seconds and distances pass. Anything measuring Essence, Coherence, resonance or Wellspring output in prose fails.
notes: Superseded by R12-1-NUMBER_BAN_STRUCK and retired outright by R12-8-VERIFY_CHECKS_RETIRED ("Checks 20 and 21 retired").

title: Whether Packs One through Seven fold into the base guides
summary: Whether to fold Packs One through Seven into the base guides, since seven unfolded packs is past the point of trackable precedence.
verbatim: Whether Packs One through Seven get folded into the base guides at last. Seven unfolded packs is past the point where precedence is trackable by reading, and Pack Seven touches four guides at once.
notes: Superseded by the same standing task restated with a growing pack count in every later pack (e.g. R19-9-STANDING_TASK).

title: Pressure suppression profiles need per-character assignment
summary: Pressure suppression profiles need assigning per named character — who can hide it, who cannot, and who stopped bothering; Sodoku and Cozbi matter most and should differ.
verbatim: Pressure suppression profiles need assigning per named character. Who can hide, who cannot, and who stopped bothering. Sodoku and Cozbi are the two that matter most and they should differ.

title: The release and true-name mechanic, pitched and unruled
summary: The release and true-name mechanic from the fifth edition's Section 6 is pitched and unruled; taking it means a naming pass per culture and rewritten first displays across the cast.
verbatim: The release and true-name mechanic from the fifth edition's Section 6 is pitched and unruled. Taking it means a naming pass per culture and rewritten first displays across the cast.
notes: This open question is what Pack Eight (still itself unratified) takes up in full; marked superseded along with the rest of the pack rather than pending, since Pack Eight has already formally addressed it.

title: The vow clause, pitched and unruled
summary: The vow clause remains pitched, unruled, and more load-bearing since narrowing is one of six escalation routes replacing bigger numbers.
verbatim: The vow clause remains pitched, unruled, and now more load-bearing, since narrowing is one of the six escalation routes that replace bigger numbers.
notes: No later pack visibly resolves this; marked superseded per the wholesale repeal default, but genuinely orphaned rather than formally settled — worth a CONFLICTS.md-style flag if a later phase finds nothing addressing it either.

title: Prose keeps every Pack Seven restriction without exception
summary: No sentence in a scene explains why a working produced its effect, no metaphysical quantities appear on the page, and the sheet's full mechanism appears in a scene only as body, room, target and cost.
verbatim: Prose retains every Pack Seven restriction without exception. No sentence in a scene explains why a working produced its effect. No metaphysical quantities on the page. The mechanism written in full on the sheet appears in a scene only as body, room, target and cost.
ratified: Isaac, 2026-09-12, Claude Code: C-003 ruled -- Twelve wins everywhere, no exceptions
notes: RULED 2026-09-12 (C-003): Pack Twelve's repeal reaches this row too. Later pack beats earlier pack, no carve-out (unlike C-001's firearms exception). Mechanism-on-the-page is the regime everywhere; this restatement is dead letter. See CONFLICTS.md and RULINGS.md.

title: The sheet explains; the page never does
summary: A character sheet, codex entry or technique writeup states the literal operation in plain functional language, with no atmosphere or withholding, so a reader can adjudicate a fight from the sheet alone.
verbatim: The sheet explains. The page never does. A character sheet, codex entry or technique writeup states the literal operation: what the ability acts on, by what process, and what result it produces. Plain functional language. No atmosphere, no withholding, no rendering the mechanism as sensation. A reader must be able to adjudicate a fight from the sheet alone.
ratified: Isaac, 2026-09-12, Claude Code ruling session: Pack Eight ratified; see CONFLICTS.md C-003 for R8-11 against Twelve

title: "Ability naming equals the phenomenon itself" repealed
summary: The Ability Guide line "ability naming equals the phenomenon itself, Ruin is Ruin" is repealed by this pack's Section Two.
verbatim: The Ability Guide line "ability naming equals the phenomenon itself, Ruin is Ruin" is repealed by Section Two below.
ratified: Isaac, 2026-09-12, Claude Code ruling session: Pack Eight ratified; see CONFLICTS.md C-003 for R8-11 against Twelve

title: The operational account moves from workbook to sheet
summary: Pack Seven's rule that the page gets only Effect/Cost/Limit/Counter and everything else stays workbook is amended: the Design Chain remains workbook, but the operational account of how an ability functions becomes sheet content.
verbatim: The Pack Seven ruling that the page gets Effect / Cost / Limit / Counter and everything else is workbook and never published is amended. The Design Chain remains workbook. The operational account of how an ability functions is now sheet content, not workbook content.
ratified: Isaac, 2026-09-12, Claude Code ruling session: Pack Eight ratified; see CONFLICTS.md C-003 for R8-11 against Twelve
notes: "The Design Chain remains workbook" is stale as of Pack Twelve §3's live restoration of the Design Chain to full prose-legal status (R12-3-DESIGN_CHAIN_RETURNS), but this row is status:proposed, so no live conflict.

title: The ten-part entry structure, in order
summary: An entry runs, in order: true name and gloss, classification block, release (where carried), description (2-6 sentences), techniques (1-3 functional lines each), cost, limit, counter (mandatory on Signature), what nobody knows, and Codex (one line at the foot).
verbatim: True name and gloss. Script where the register has one, romanisation, literal English meaning in parentheses, then the by-name if the art has earned one.
ratified: Isaac, 2026-09-12, Claude Code ruling session: Pack Eight ratified; see CONFLICTS.md C-003 for R8-11 against Twelve
notes: This is an "entry" (an art, potentially with several named techniques under it), a different granularity from Pack Twelve/Seventeen's per-technique summary card; possible overlap not reconciled by any pack's own text, so no supersedes/amends contradiction is asserted either way.

title: The eight-field classification block, nothing invented
summary: Class (Offensive/Defensive/Supplementary), Family (one of the Eight), Wellspring (from the Sixty, primary first), Method (one of eight named methods), Physics Domain (one of the Nine), Grade (fixed Tier Grade scale), Range (real units), and Medium — all drawn from live WOTR taxonomy, nothing invented.
verbatim: Eight fields, all drawn from live WOTR taxonomy. Nothing invented. Class · Family · Wellspring · Method · Physics Domain · Grade · Range · Medium
ratified: Isaac, 2026-09-12, Claude Code ruling session: Pack Eight ratified; see CONFLICTS.md C-003 for R8-11 against Twelve

title: The description is written as a manual entry
summary: The description is written the way a man teaching it would write it: flat operational prose, no mood, no cadence work, no elegiac register — that belongs in scenes.
verbatim: Written the way a man who has to teach it would write it. How the resource divides, what the working acts on, what the target experiences, what breaks it, what happens when it fails. Flat operational prose. No mood, no cadence work, no elegiac register. That belongs in scenes.
ratified: Isaac, 2026-09-12, Claude Code ruling session: Pack Eight ratified; see CONFLICTS.md C-003 for R8-11 against Twelve

title: "Overuse strains him" always fails
summary: "Overuse strains him" remains a failing drawback and always was.
verbatim: "Overuse strains him" remains a failure and always was.
ratified: Isaac, 2026-09-12, Claude Code ruling session: Pack Eight ratified; see CONFLICTS.md C-003 for R8-11 against Twelve

title: Drawback numbers are physical, never metaphysical
summary: Drawback numbers are physical (metres, seconds, kilograms, degrees, counts, durations); never a number attached to Essence, Coherence, resonance or Wellspring output — Pack Seven's metaphysical-units ban holds on the sheet as firmly as on the page.
verbatim: Numbers where the number is physical: metres, seconds, kilograms, degrees, counts, durations. Never a number attached to Essence, Coherence, resonance or Wellspring output. Pack Seven's ban on metaphysical units holds on the sheet as firmly as on the page.
ratified: Isaac, 2026-09-12, Claude Code ruling session: Pack Eight ratified; see CONFLICTS.md C-003 for R8-11 against Twelve

title: This pack's own first draft of Section Two is repealed
summary: Pack Eight Section Two's first draft, which set the naming language by filing body, is repealed by the version in this file.
verbatim: Repeals Pack Eight Section Two's first draft, which set the language by filing body.
ratified: Isaac, 2026-09-12, Claude Code ruling session: Pack Eight ratified; see CONFLICTS.md C-003 for R8-11 against Twelve
notes: The repealed first draft is not a separate file in sources/ — only this final version exists in the corpus — so no supersedes id target exists to point at.

title: A true name belongs to the practitioner's own language
summary: The true name is in the practitioner's own language; neither the Accord, the Guild, nor the Family has a claim on it, and a register's Latin gloss never appears in the practitioner's own mouth.
verbatim: The true name is in the practitioner's own language. The Accord has no claim on it, and neither does the Guild or the Family. A Ketsuen swordsman inducted into the Accord does not rename his house's work in Latin because a clerk in Stannvaard needs it alphabetised.
ratified: Isaac, 2026-09-12, Claude Code ruling session: Pack Eight ratified; see CONFLICTS.md C-003 for R8-11 against Twelve

title: Naming registers are not ethnicity
summary: A Japonic-sounding name is evidence about a house's linguistic descent and nothing else; this ruling is unchanged from elsewhere.
verbatim: Naming registers are not ethnicity. This ruling is unchanged. A Japonic-sounding name is evidence about a house's linguistic descent, nothing else.
ratified: Isaac, 2026-09-12, Claude Code ruling session: Pack Eight ratified; see CONFLICTS.md C-003 for R8-11 against Twelve
notes: "This ruling is unchanged" implies an existing rule stated elsewhere in the base guides, not newly introduced here; no source in this corpus states it first, so no supersedes/amends target is asserted.

title: Naming register by practitioner origin
summary: Where a request specifies a register, that register governs and the name is built in it first: Concord/Accord/Guild/Sanctum Lux is Latinate; Ketsuen/Japonic houses use Japanese; Korean-register houses use Korean; Büri is Mongolian; Dawi is stressed Germanic-Norse compound; Eresse is Latinate with elvish morphology; Parunic and older strata use Parun etymology.
verbatim: Where a request specifies a register, that register governs, and the name is built in it before anything else about the ability is decided. Japonic ask, Japonic name. Korean ask, Korean name.
ratified: Isaac, 2026-09-12, Claude Code ruling session: Pack Eight ratified; see CONFLICTS.md C-003 for R8-11 against Twelve

title: The by-name is where poetry is allowed to live
summary: The by-name, where an art has one, sits after the gloss and is what other characters call it — the one place poetry is allowed.
verbatim: The by-name, where an art has one, sits after the gloss and is what other characters call it. That is where the poetry is allowed to live.
ratified: Isaac, 2026-09-12, Claude Code ruling session: Pack Eight ratified; see CONFLICTS.md C-003 for R8-11 against Twelve

title: The gloss is flat and literal, never poetic
summary: The gloss is the true name's plain English meaning, flat and literal, no poetry or interpretation; if the literal meaning is dull, the name is wrong and gets rebuilt rather than dressed up.
verbatim: True name, then plain English meaning in parentheses. Kagemusha reads Shadow Warrior. It does not read the technique of hidden purpose. Flat, literal, no poetry, no interpretation. If the literal meaning is dull, the name is wrong and gets rebuilt, and the gloss is never used to dress it up.
ratified: Isaac, 2026-09-12, Claude Code ruling session: Pack Eight ratified; see CONFLICTS.md C-003 for R8-11 against Twelve

title: Art carries the character; techniques do not
summary: Naming runs art, then technique, then form; the art carries the character and is spoken once at release then assumed, while individual techniques are spoken every time they are used.
verbatim: Art, then technique, then form. The art carries the character. Individual techniques may not. An art is spoken once at release and thereafter assumed. Techniques are spoken every time they are used.
ratified: Isaac, 2026-09-12, Claude Code ruling session: Pack Eight ratified; see CONFLICTS.md C-003 for R8-11 against Twelve

title: The release, an optional imperative call
summary: An art with a true name may carry a release call (imperative verb plus name); it is never required for the art to function, costs a beat for a measurable output increase, and is spoken indistinguishably by a man in real danger or a man showing off.
verbatim: An art with a true name may carry a call: an imperative verb plus the name. - The release is never required for the art to function. - Speaking it costs a beat and buys a measurable increase in output. - The man in real danger says it and the man showing off says it, and the difference is not visible from outside.
ratified: Isaac, 2026-09-12, Claude Code ruling session: Pack Eight ratified; see CONFLICTS.md C-003 for R8-11 against Twelve

title: New names are for new arts only
summary: A stronger expression of a known art takes a modifier on the existing true name; new names are reserved for genuinely new arts.
verbatim: A stronger expression of a known art takes a modifier on the existing true name. New names are for new arts only.
ratified: Isaac, 2026-09-12, Claude Code ruling session: Pack Eight ratified; see CONFLICTS.md C-003 for R8-11 against Twelve

title: A working that needs its meaning glossed has failed
summary: A working whose meaning must be glossed for the scene to land is a working that failed; fix the working, not the gloss.
verbatim: A working whose meaning must be glossed for the scene to land is a working that failed. Fix the working.
ratified: Isaac, 2026-09-12, Claude Code ruling session: Pack Eight ratified; see CONFLICTS.md C-003 for R8-11 against Twelve

title: The gloss never appears in prose
summary: The gloss never appears in prose, with no translation apposition; the reader gets it from the sheet or from another character explaining it in dialogue for their own reason.
verbatim: The gloss never appears in prose. No translation apposition. No he spoke the words that meant. The reader takes the gloss from the sheet, or from another character explaining it in dialogue for a reason of their own.
ratified: Isaac, 2026-09-12, Claude Code ruling session: Pack Eight ratified; see CONFLICTS.md C-003 for R8-11 against Twelve

title: A true name is spoken, never narrated
summary: The true name is spoken by a character; it never appears in narration.
verbatim: The true name is spoken by a character. It never appears in narration.
ratified: Isaac, 2026-09-12, Claude Code ruling session: Pack Eight ratified; see CONFLICTS.md C-003 for R8-11 against Twelve

title: Nobody translates their own technique aloud
summary: Nobody translates their own technique's name aloud, ever.
verbatim: Nobody translates their own technique aloud. Ever.
ratified: Isaac, 2026-09-12, Claude Code ruling session: Pack Eight ratified; see CONFLICTS.md C-003 for R8-11 against Twelve

title: One release per scene at most
summary: One release per scene at most; two men releasing in the same scene is an event, not texture.
verbatim: One release per scene at most. Two men releasing in the same scene is an event, not texture.
ratified: Isaac, 2026-09-12, Claude Code ruling session: Pack Eight ratified; see CONFLICTS.md C-003 for R8-11 against Twelve

title: Standing task, a naming pass per culture
summary: A naming pass runs per culture; existing techniques already established in prose are flagged, not renamed, cashing the release-and-true-name mechanic pitched since the fifth edition and requiring rewritten first displays across the major cast.
verbatim: Naming pass per culture. Existing techniques already established in prose are flagged, not renamed. This cashes the release-and-true-name mechanic that has been sitting pitched on the docket since the fifth edition, and it means rewritten first displays across the major cast.
ratified: Isaac, 2026-09-12, Claude Code ruling session: Pack Eight ratified; see CONFLICTS.md C-003 for R8-11 against Twelve

title: AUCTORITAS and KŌMYAKU, worked entries pending ratification
summary: Two full worked entries (AUCTORITAS in Latin register, KŌMYAKU in Japanese register) demonstrate the new entry format; per the Ratification Ledger, nothing in them is canon until Isaac rules, and the Division's "four hundred and six" catalogued errata count is explicitly self-flagged as an invented, unsized figure.
verbatim: Two entries in the format, in different registers, to fix the shape.
ratified: Isaac, 2026-09-12, Claude Code ruling session: Pack Eight ratified; see CONFLICTS.md C-003 for R8-11 against Twelve
notes: Full technique flavour text for AUCTORITAS and KŌMYAKU is not extracted row by row — worked-example content per BRIEF, not enforceable rule text.

title: The retroactive work, five tasks folded into the cost audit
summary: Folded into the cost audit: re-cut every existing technique entry into the §1.3 structure; add a classification block to every entry from live taxonomy only, flagging any entry with no legal Codex combination; run the §2.1 naming pass per culture, flagging prose-established names rather than renaming; run a drawback pass checking every Cost line against the overuse-strains-him test and the metaphysical-units ban; write Counter lines onto every Signature technique that lacks one.
verbatim: Folds into the cost audit instead of running as a separate pass.
ratified: Isaac, 2026-09-12, Claude Code ruling session: Pack Eight ratified; see CONFLICTS.md C-003 for R8-11 against Twelve
notes: "Priority target: Niran" (source line 197) is a work-prioritisation diagnostic on one character's kit, not extracted — consistent with skipping other packs' retrospective priority lists.

title: The four-media Craft structure is confirmed canon
summary: Magicraft, Spellcraft, Runecraft and Draftcraft are confirmed canon as the naming scheme for how a working is performed; Chantcraft stays pending.
verbatim: The four-media structure — Magicraft, Spellcraft, Runecraft, Draftcraft — is confirmed canon as the naming scheme for how a working gets performed. Chantcraft stays pending.
ratified: Ratified by Isaac's direction, live this session

title: Craft-structure items this pack leaves undecided
summary: Chantcraft accept/reject/fold, the Law V gate (Stage VII proposed), Law III's rewrite, whether Runecraft outranks Spellcraft everywhere or by culture, the golden-age question, and the Latinate/vernacular doublet's scope are all still Isaac's to rule; the Ratification Ledger separately reconfirms Chantcraft, the Law V gate, status inversion by culture, and per-faction Visual Aesthetic Guide passes as still open.
verbatim: Still open, not decided by this pack, and not to be treated as resolved: Chantcraft accept/reject/fold, the Law V gate (Stage VII proposed), Law III's rewrite, whether Runecraft outranks Spellcraft everywhere or by culture, the golden-age question, and the scope of the Latinate/vernacular doublet. All flagged in the source document's Part Four docket and still Isaac's to rule.
notes: RULED 2026-09-12 (two of the items): Chantcraft is folded into Spellcraft, not a fifth craft; Runecraft outranks Spellcraft by culture, not everywhere. RULED 2026-09-12, later: the Law V gate is confirmed at Stage VII, as proposed. Still open: Law III's rewrite, the golden-age question, the Latinate/vernacular doublet's scope.

title: Which craft word a mouth reaches for is class-marking
summary: Which word a character uses for a craft is characterisation: an Engraver says "the cutting," a Kharven soldier says "a man who can do the writing," and nobody says "Runecraft" aloud except an Accord examiner filling in a form.
verbatim: Which word a mouth reaches for is characterisation: an Engraver says the cutting. A Kharven soldier wanting help says he needs a man who can do the writing. Nobody says "Runecraft" aloud except an Accord examiner filling in a form.
ratified: Ratified by Isaac's direction, live this session
notes: This is the class-marking-by-vocabulary rule Pack Fifteen §4 later demotes from requirement to optional flavour (see R15-4-PACK_NINE_CLASS_MARKING).

title: Common-tongue craft naming is prose-legal
summary: A POV may be shown cutting a ward, speaking a working, or pouring a Draft (singing pending Chantcraft's ruling); the common tongue for craft actions is prose-legal, said the way the character would actually say it, while the Accord Latin terms stay document-only.

ratified: Ratified by Isaac's direction, live this session

title: The mechanism-gloss and metaphysical-unit bans are untouched

verbatim: Untouched by this pack: the mechanism gloss ban (Check 20), the metaphysical-units ban (Check 21), the chemistry ban, the rule that Effect stays physical. A line may say a man cut a ward into the doorframe. It may not say why the cutting suppressed the Essence.
ratified: Ratified by Isaac's direction, live this session

verbatim: Aura as fracture, not glow. Where Essence discharge needs a visual, it reads as broken geometry around the body — jagged, shard-edged light, not a soft radiant bloom. "It glowed" stays banned; this is its replacement specifically for a Stage-display beat, not a general substitute for the phenomenon bank.
ratified: Ratified by Isaac's direction, live this session

title: The body under load, one splash-panel beat per scene

verbatim: The body under load. A Pressure spike or a peak-effort feat is rendered as visible physical distortion — vein, tendon, muscle read exaggerated under strain, ink-dense the way a splash panel goes dense at the one panel that matters. WOTR is licensed exactly one splash-panel beat per scene, at the display, never twice.
ratified: Ratified by Isaac's direction, live this session

title: Ignorance quota, misreading budget and one-read rule still bind

verbatim: Cost, unchanged. The ignorance quota, the misreading budget, and the one-read Apparatus Rule still bind a Stage-display beat exactly as hard as any other scene.
ratified: Ratified by Isaac's direction, live this session
