verbatim: Eyes as the tell. At a Stage threshold or a dropped suppression, the eyes go first — light behind them rather than in them, overtaking iris and sclera both. Rendered as a fact the room reacts to; the Apparatus Rule still applies, one read and then silence.
ratified: Ratified by Isaac's direction, live this session

title: The power-display register applies to a narrow beat list only
summary: The new power-display register applies only to Stage-ascension beats, a Pressure drop, and a technique's first display or finisher; the Visual Aesthetic Guide's grounded North Star governs everywhere else (wounds, environment, objects, ordinary combat, material culture).
verbatim: Scope, and it is narrow on purpose. This applies only to Stage-ascension beats, a Pressure drop, and a technique's first display or finisher — the same short list the Ability Guide and Pack Seven already flag for the physical standard (what the body did, what the room did, what the target felt, what it cost). Everywhere else — wounds, environment, objects, ordinary combat, material culture — the Visual Aesthetic Guide's Berserk/Vinland grounded North Star stands untouched.
ratified: Ratified by Isaac's direction, live this session
notes: "The Berserk/Vinland grounded North Star stands untouched" is stale as of Pack Eleven §1, which retires that North Star entirely (R11-1-NORTH_STAR_RETIRED); no supersedes link is set since Eleven's text retires the North Star generally and never cites Pack Nine PART THREE by name.

title: Silhouette-first entrance licensed for power-arrival
summary: A practitioner arriving at an unclassified Pressure is staged backlit, shape before detail, using the existing Section 3 silhouette tool now explicitly licensed for power-arrival rather than rationed to dread generally.
verbatim: Silhouette-first entrance. A practitioner arriving at a Pressure the room hasn't classified yet is staged backlit, shape before detail — the existing silhouette tool in Section 3, now explicitly licensed for a power-arrival rather than rationed to dread generally.
ratified: Ratified by Isaac's direction, live this session

title: The 26 Magical Categories ratified as a second axis
summary: The Magical Categories (Arts, Drafts, Conjunction, Synergia, Harmonia, Ritus, Phenomena, Glyphica, Manifestus, Viaforma, Traitus, Mechanica, Crystalia, Wellsprings, Animatria, Vocatia, Vectra, Mnemata, Aetherica, Concordia, Domain Weaving, Claustra, Silentia, Auguria, Transitus, Votia) are ratified as live canon, answering what kind of thing a working is, alongside the Four Crafts' answer of how it is performed.
verbatim: The Magical Categories answer what kind of thing it is — Arts, Drafts, Conjunction, Synergia, Harmonia, Ritus, Phenomena, Glyphica, Manifestus, Viaforma, Traitus, Mechanica, Crystalia, Wellsprings, Animatria, Vocatia, Vectra, Mnemata, Aetherica, Concordia, Domain Weaving, Claustra, Silentia, Auguria, Transitus, Votia.
ratified: Ratified by Isaac's direction, live this session
notes: Pack Ten beats Pack Nine where they overlap and extends it everywhere else (source line 5); a general precedence statement, not a specific quoted strike, so no supersedes link is set against any Pack Nine row.

title: Craft is the mouth; Category is the shape
summary: Craft and Category cross like Family and Method at a coarser grain — Craft is the mouth a working comes out of, Category is the shape of the thing that comes out; the same category can be delivered by different crafts with different results.
verbatim: The two cross the same way Family and Method already do, at a coarser grain: Craft is the mouth it comes out of. Category is the shape of the thing that comes out.
ratified: Ratified by Isaac's direction, live this session

title: The Apparatus Rule's one read may name a category instead
summary: A scene's single diagnostic read (the Apparatus Rule's existing budget, not a new one) may be spent naming the category instead of a Wellspring or Family; naming a category doesn't trip Check 20, but it still costs the scene's only read.
verbatim: One exception, and it is the Apparatus Rule's existing budget, not a new one. A scene's single explicit diagnostic read may be spent naming the category instead of naming a Wellspring or Family — a scholar, examiner, or rival practitioner gets one line: "That's Animatria. It isn't a real animal." Naming a category is not accounting for why it works, so it does not trip Check 20. It still costs the scene's only read, and after it the faculty goes silent same as always.
ratified: Ratified by Isaac's direction, live this session
notes: This budget is later struck outright by Pack Twelve §7 (R12-7-APPARATUS_CAP_REPLACED, replacing the one-read cap with a tempo cost); no supersedes link is set here since the underlying target (the Apparatus Rule itself) isn't identified by a specific Pack Six rule id yet — confirm and cross-reference once Pack Six is extracted.

title: Category names default to workbook and Codex-line only
summary: Category names sit at Wellspring/Family register, not common tongue, and stay workbook and Codex-line by default.
verbatim: Category names (Animatria, Manifestus, Vectra, and so on) sit at Wellspring/Family register, not common-tongue register — nobody calls a tiger "my Animatria" the way a soldier says "the writing." They stay workbook and Codex-line by default.
ratified: Ratified by Isaac's direction, live this session

title: Animatria — directed, semi-independent, line-dependent
summary: An Animatria shape moves with the caster's active attention, can obey or strain against instruction, and stops being anything if the live line back to its maker is severed (Silence, a killed caster, a broken focus).
verbatim: Animatria — the shape is directed and semi-independent. It moves with intent the caster is actively spending attention on, it can obey or strain against instruction, and its continuity depends on a live line back to whoever made it — sever that line (Silence, a killed caster, a broken focus) and it stops being anything.
ratified: Ratified by Isaac's direction, live this session

title: The delivering craft sets the projected shape's durability
summary: Spellcraft holds only while attention holds; Runecraft is fixed and degrades like any inscription; Draftcraft is bottled, cruder, and buyer-triggerable; Chantcraft requires the sustaining choir and is pending Chantcraft's own ruling.
verbatim: The delivering craft sets how much the shape can be trusted to hold:
ratified: Ratified by Isaac's direction, live this session
notes: The Chantcraft row is conditional on Chantcraft's accept/reject ruling, still open per the Ratification Ledger; check whether Pack Nine (Phase 2) carries a formal R-coded open ruling for it, and cross-reference here if so.

title: A projected shape's Effect is physical only, never causal
summary: A projected shape's Effect describes only what it looks/does/feels like, never why the Wellspring resolved as that particular shape; if that answer exists at all, it stays workbook, one line, never on the page.
verbatim: Effect is physical only. What the shape looks like, what it does, what the room and the target feel. Never why the Wellspring resolved as a tiger and not a wolf — if that answer exists at all, it is workbook, one line at the foot, never on the page.
ratified: Ratified by Isaac's direction, live this session

title: Manifestus — involuntary, short-lived, a Trait bleeding through
summary: A Manifestus shape is involuntary, arriving on a pressure or emotion spike, short-lived by nature, and reads as a Trait bleeding through rather than a tool being used; nobody aimed it.
verbatim: Manifestus — the shape is involuntary. It arrives on a pressure or emotion spike, is short-lived by nature, and reads as a Trait bleeding through rather than a tool being used. Nobody aimed it. It came out.
ratified: Ratified by Isaac's direction, live this session

title: Ability Effect may render as an externalised shape
summary: Ability Effect fields may render a working as an externalised shape (animal, elemental figure, guardian silhouette) instead of only as discharge, pressure, or weather.
verbatim: This is the change Isaac asked for directly. Ability Effect fields may now render a working as an externalized shape — animal, elemental figure, guardian silhouette — instead of only as discharge, pressure, or weather.
ratified: Ratified by Isaac's direction, live this session

title: Traitus — passive, permanent, condition-gated visibility
summary: A Traitus shape is passive and permanent, not fired or summoned but a standing mark of what the Crystal has become, visible only under a specific condition and gone the instant that condition lapses.
verbatim: Traitus — the shape is passive and permanent. Not fired, not summoned — a standing mark of what the Crystal has become, visible only under a specific condition (a clenched fist, a raised pulse) and gone the instant that condition lapses.
ratified: Ratified by Isaac's direction, live this session

title: Splash-panel, read budget and ignorance quota still govern
summary: A projected shape still counts toward the one splash-panel beat per scene (Pack Nine), still costs the one diagnostic read per scene if the category is named, and the ignorance quota/misreading budget are untouched — a POV may see a projected shape and get it wrong.
verbatim: - One splash-panel beat per scene (Pack Nine) still governs the moment the shape is at its most visually loud. - One diagnostic read per scene (Part Two above) still governs any naming of the category itself. - Ignorance quota and misreading budget are untouched.
ratified: Ratified by Isaac's direction, live this session

title: The Berserk/Vinland visual North Star is retired
summary: The grounded Berserk/Vinland Saga visual North Star in the Visual Aesthetic Guide is retired.
verbatim: Confirmed by Isaac's direction. The grounded Berserk / Vinland Saga visual North Star in the Visual Aesthetic Guide is retired. It was a mud-and-mail costume on a world that files paperwork about magic.

title: Reference triangle and the widened power-display register
summary: Warhammer 40,000 for bureaucratic scale, late-Victorian industrial imperialism for material texture and class geography, and manhwa for visual power-display grammar — the last now widened from Pack Nine's four beat types to the general visual register. References are not to be imitated directly.
verbatim: Reference triangle, not to be imitated: Warhammer 40,000 for the scale of the bureaucracy and the sense that the machinery outlived its explanation. Late-Victorian industrial imperialism for the material texture, class geography, and the survey-and-annex habit. Manhwa for the visual grammar of power display, per Pack Nine, now widened from four beat types to the general visual register.

title: The Draw-Age visual register
summary: The new visual register is an imperial age built on a resource nobody can see, administered by a measuring guild, defended by men in proofed plate carrying both sword and firearm.
verbatim: An imperial age built on a resource nobody can see, administered by a guild that measures it, defended by men in proofed plate who carry both a sword and a firearm because each answers a different threat.

title: Pack Eleven widens the look, not the sound
summary: Pack Five stands in full; the Western Register still governs characterisation, humour and narration authority. Pack Eleven widens what the page may look like, not what it may sound like.
verbatim: Tonal spine unchanged. Pack Five stands in full. The Western Register governs characterisation, humour, and narration authority. Pack Eleven widens what the page may look like. It does not reopen what the page may sound like. Temür still does not make jokes.
notes: Confirms Pack Five's non-register-by-culture provisions (dramatic irony, elegiac mode, humour, narration authority) as still governing; consistent with R15-4-PACK_FIVE_SCOPE, no conflict.

title: Apparatus inherits its Family's failure modes
summary: A machine is a conduit retuned to a current (phase-locking, not restricted to souls); every apparatus inherits its Family's favoured condition, suppressive condition, and characteristic pathology off the Environmental Coupling table.
verbatim: Apparatus harmonizes the way a practitioner does. Phase-locking is the canon mechanism and it is not restricted to souls. A machine is a conduit retuned to a current. Therefore every apparatus inherits its Family's favoured condition, suppressive condition, and characteristic pathology straight off the Environmental Coupling table.
ratified: Isaac, 2026-09-12, Claude Code ruling session: the originated parts of Pack Eleven ratified with the packs already confirmed

title: Class geography follows draw distance from a site
summary: A city's street plan follows where the current runs shallowest; the rich live over the pool, the poor live at the thin margin where lamps gutter through the Thin Weeks.
verbatim: Cities sit on sites, not on rivers. A seat's street plan is dictated by where the current runs shallowest. Draw falls off with distance from the site. The rich live over the pool. The poor live at the margin where output is thin and the lamps gutter through the Thin Weeks.
ratified: Isaac, 2026-09-12, Claude Code ruling session: the originated parts of Pack Eleven ratified with the packs already confirmed

title: Drawdown is the imperial motive
summary: Old World veins are worked; New World veins are pristine; colonial expansion has a hydrological cause, wars fought over water tables no eye can see.
verbatim: Drawdown is the imperial motive. Old World veins are worked. The New World's are pristine at densities the Old World has not seen since the Antediluvian Calendar, because nobody has been drawing. Colonial expansion with a hydrological cause.
ratified: Isaac, 2026-09-12, Claude Code ruling session: the originated parts of Pack Eleven ratified with the packs already confirmed

title: The industrial age is hydrology, not combustion
summary: The technological age runs on Wellsprings as standing currents that pool where substrate/competing-currents/time allow, per The Mechanism of the Sixty; nobody built an engine, they sank a well.
verbatim: So the industrial age is not combustion. It is hydrology. Nobody built an engine. They sank a well, put a town around it, and grew a guild that decides who may sink another.
ratified: Isaac, 2026-09-12, Claude Code ruling session: the originated parts of Pack Eleven ratified with the packs already confirmed

title: The Measurewrights maintain the Draw without explaining it
summary: The Guild of Measurewrights (Hexagonal Oath, in concurrence with Research & Archives) wrote the address down but does not explain the mechanism.
verbatim: The Measurewrights are the order that maintains it. Guild of Measurewrights, under the Hexagonal Oath, already canon, already in concurrence with Research & Archives. They wrote the address down. They do not explain it, and Pack Seven means they never will.
ratified: Isaac, 2026-09-12, Claude Code ruling session: the originated parts of Pack Eleven ratified with the packs already confirmed
notes: "Pack Seven means they never will" cites a now-repealed pack (R12-1-PACK_SEVEN_REPEALED); the practical outcome likely survives anyway under Pack Twelve S6's Mystic Register (rules stated as rules, unexplained — the Measurewrights read as a paradigm Mystic Register voice), but the citation itself is stale. Not raised as a CONFLICTS.md row since this whole row is status:proposed, not live, so nothing live actually contradicts.

title: The Draw-Age silhouette, sensory texture
summary: No smokestacks or soot; standpipes, gauge-housings, sealed conduit, brass and slate and Guild seals, a district's low draw-hum, and the politically loaded silence when a district's draw is cut.
verbatim: Silhouette. No smokestacks, no soot, no coal. Instead: standpipes and gauge-housings, sealed conduit run along building faces like plumbing, brass and slate and Guild seals, the constant low draw-hum of a district that is drinking, and the sudden silence when a district's draw is cut. That silence is a political act and everyone in earshot knows it.
ratified: Isaac, 2026-09-12, Claude Code ruling session: the originated parts of Pack Eleven ratified with the packs already confirmed

title: Common-tongue vs Guild-register draw vocabulary
summary: "The draw, the hum, a standpipe, a housing, the meter, cut off" are common-tongue and prose-legal under Pack Nine's craft-register carve-out; "concentration, density, coupling, eta" are Guild register and document-only.
verbatim: Vocabulary, common tongue, prose-legal under Pack Nine's craft-register carve-out: the draw, the hum, a standpipe, a housing, the meter, cut off. Guild register, document-only: concentration, density, coupling, eta.
ratified: Isaac, 2026-09-12, Claude Code ruling session: the originated parts of Pack Eleven ratified with the packs already confirmed

title: The three ammunition tiers
summary: Common shot (cheap, kills men, annoys practitioners), proofed shot (Materia-coupled, Guild-stamped, defeats proofed plate but not a Domain), and the named round (one-shot assassination ordnance, Wellspring-coupled and paid for in advance).
verbatim: The three ammunition tiers, originated, pending ruling:
ratified: Isaac, 2026-09-12, Claude Code ruling session: the originated parts of Pack Eleven ratified with the packs already confirmed

title: Why plate stops shrinking in WOTR
summary: Shot is chemically cheap and does not care about a soul; a working is not shot, so mass and material still buy a fraction of a second against a Wellspring-carried strike, which is why armour retreats to the cuirass-and-helm silhouette and stops there.
verbatim: Shot is chemically cheap and does not care what a man's soul is doing. A working is not shot. Against a Wellspring-carried strike, mass and material still buy the fraction of a second in which a man can be somewhere else. So armour retreats to the historical cuirass-and-helm silhouette and then stops there, because the last article you would take off is the one standing between your chest and something that was not there a moment ago.

title: Powder weapons open an engagement, they do not decide one
summary: Powder weapons are slow, loud and honest; a practitioner above roughly the middle Stages is not reliably killed by common shot, which is why the enchanted round exists at the cost it does.
verbatim: Ballistics ruling. Powder weapons are slow, loud, and honest. They open an engagement, they do not decide one. A practitioner above roughly the middle Stages is not reliably killed by common shot, which is precisely why the enchanted round exists and precisely why it costs what a family earns in a season.

title: Every armed man carries sword and firearm
summary: The silhouette is coat, breast, helm, sword and firearm; every armed man carries at least two answers because there are at least two questions, which is why the Combat Craft Guide survives intact — Liechtenauer and Fiore still govern inside twenty feet.
verbatim: Result: the silhouette is coat, breast, helm, sword, and firearm. Every armed man carries at least two answers because there are at least two questions. This is why the Combat Craft Guide survives intact. Liechtenauer and Fiore still govern. Inside twenty feet a discharged firearm is a club and the sword is the thing that finishes it.

title: No sentence explains why a proofed round defeats plate
summary: The gun is furniture, not spectacle; no sentence explains why a proofed round defeats proofed plate — the physical account of the hole stays, the causal account is cut.
verbatim: Prose law for firearms. The gun is furniture, not spectacle. Powder smells of rotten egg and it stays in the wool for days. Misfires are common in wet weather and a soldier's relationship with his own weapon is superstitious and practical at once. No sentence explains why a proofed round defeats a proofed plate. The physical account of the hole stays. The causal account is cut, per Pack Seven.
notes: C-001 ruled 2026-09-12: Eleven's ban stands. No sentence explains why a proofed round defeats proofed plate, even after Twelve's general repeal; firearms are the carve-out from mechanism-on-the-page.

title: Gunpowder, magic and armour all coexist
summary: Gunpowder exists, magical weapons exist, and armour is not dead.
verbatim: Confirmed by Isaac's direction: gunpowder exists. Magical weapons exist. Armour is not dead.

title: Proof-marks are canon texture
summary: A dented cuirass is certified rather than damaged; soldiers read a proof-dent the way Kharven reads a forearm grip, and a shallow proof-dent signals a light charge and what that means about the man wearing it.
verbatim: Proof-marks are canon texture from this pack forward. A dented cuirass is certified rather than damaged, and a soldier reads another soldier's dent the way Kharven reads a forearm grip. Armour whose proof-dent is shallow was proofed with a light charge, and everyone knows what that means about the man wearing it.

title: Depth axis: the nested plane model
summary: A Well is not a hole in the ground; it is a place where the surface (Physical) has thinned enough that the middle layer (Soul) reaches through toward Fate, the deepest plane.
verbatim: Depth, the nested plane model. Fate deepest, Soul between, Physical at the surface. A Well is not a hole in the ground. It is a place where the surface has thinned enough that the middle layer reaches through.
ratified: Isaac, 2026-09-12, Claude Code ruling session: the originated parts of Pack Eleven ratified with the packs already confirmed

title: A descent's sensory opening inverts toward the body
summary: A descent's sensory opening favours the body (feet, teeth, pack weight) over the room; the ignorance quota becomes the ambient condition rather than a per-scene quota, and a misidentified encounter type is the best-shaped disaster the setting offers.
verbatim: Sensory opening inverts toward the body, not the room: what the feet report, what the teeth taste, what the pack's weight is doing. The ignorance quota is not a quota inside a Well, it is the ambient condition. The Apparatus Rule still holds at one read per scene and it should usually be spent wrong, because a misidentified encounter type is the best-shaped disaster available in this setting.
ratified: Isaac, 2026-09-12, Claude Code ruling session: the originated parts of Pack Eleven ratified with the packs already confirmed
notes: "The Apparatus Rule still holds at one read per scene" is now stale against the live R12-7-APPARATUS_CAP_REPLACED, which struck that cap; not raised as a CONFLICTS.md row since this whole row is status:proposed (unconfirmed), not live, so nothing live actually contradicts Twelve.

title: Direction axis: Wild, Spirit and Medium-type Wells
summary: Wild-type Wells make the environment the enemy (Materia/Spatium dominant); Spirit-type make the Crystal the enemy, authoring the delver from inside (Caloria/Fulguria/some Vectoria) and kill experienced parties; Medium-type are both reciprocally, the largest survey gap.
verbatim: Direction, the encounter type. This is the whole design grammar and it is better than a monster list.
ratified: Isaac, 2026-09-12, Claude Code ruling session: the originated parts of Pack Eleven ratified with the packs already confirmed

title: Magnitude axis: density scale, never invent an intermediate rung
summary: Magnitude runs Ambient through Core with attested rungs (Ambient Saturation, Active Concentration, Veil-Thin, Core); intermediate rungs must be pulled from source before use and never invented.
verbatim: Magnitude, the density scale. Runs Ambient through Core. Attested rungs: Ambient Saturation, Active Concentration, Veil-Thin, Core. Flag: the intermediate rungs need pulling from source before any scene uses them. Never invent one.
ratified: Isaac, 2026-09-12, Claude Code ruling session: the originated parts of Pack Eleven ratified with the packs already confirmed

title: The Well survey protocol, seven rules as plot devices
summary: Deploy in pairs with one member outside the radius; take Crystal baselines before the march, never after; never carry Object Wellsprings into Site Wellsprings; withdrawal is not retreat; report Medium-type as priority; every rule is one a character can break, and the Guild has buried those who did.
verbatim: The survey protocol is already written and is pure scene structure. On Walking Into the Current gives seven rules and every one of them is a plot device. Deploy in pairs with one member outside the radius, because the external observer is the only reliable instrument. Take Crystal baselines before the march, never after. Do not carry Object Wellsprings into Site Wellsprings. Two laws sharing one Shell, unpredictable and frequently catastrophic. Withdrawal is not retreat. Report Medium-type as priority.
ratified: Isaac, 2026-09-12, Claude Code ruling session: the originated parts of Pack Eleven ratified with the packs already confirmed
notes: The "Object Wellsprings into Site Wellsprings" rule is the same canon example Pack Twelve S6 uses for Mystic Register grammar (see R12-6-RULES_AS_RULES); consistent restatement, not a duplicate rule or a conflict.

title: Wells are extraction, never adventure
summary: A Core-density Well is the richest draw site that exists; the Guild licenses descents, the Accord taxes them, chartered companies fund them, and delvers are paid like miners — sack-and-contribution logic, no treasure chest.
verbatim: What the Wells are economically. Extraction, and never adventure. A Well at Core density is the richest draw site that exists and the reason it has not been sunk is that the survey team keeps not coming back. So the Guild licenses descents, the Accord taxes them, chartered companies fund them, and the delvers who go down are paid like miners, which is to say badly and with a bonus that their widow collects. Sack-and-contribution logic. The treasure chest does not exist here.
ratified: Isaac, 2026-09-12, Claude Code ruling session: the originated parts of Pack Eleven ratified with the packs already confirmed

title: A Well is where the landscape has become the law's argument
summary: At sufficient concentration, a law the landscape has been measured by for so long that the landscape has become the law's argument, per The Mechanism of the Sixty.
verbatim: Originated, pending ruling. Derived from canon, not imported from the genre.
ratified: Isaac, 2026-09-12, Claude Code ruling session: the originated parts of Pack Eleven ratified with the packs already confirmed

title: Guild register vs common tongue for a Well
summary: Guild register calls it a Core Concentration; common tongue calls it a Well; going in is a descent, and the people who do it are delvers or well-rats.
verbatim: Guild register: a Core Concentration. Common tongue: a Well. Going in is a descent. The people who do it are delvers, or well-rats if you dislike them, which most people do.
ratified: Isaac, 2026-09-12, Claude Code ruling session: the originated parts of Pack Eleven ratified with the packs already confirmed

title: An engagement may open at range before HEMA grammar takes over
summary: The Combat Craft Guide is unchanged in substance, with the addition that an engagement may open at range and the HEMA grammar takes over inside roughly twenty feet.
verbatim: WOTR_Combat_Craft_Guide.md. Unchanged in substance. Add: an engagement may open at range and the HEMA grammar takes over inside roughly twenty feet.

title: Kharven's Standing Inventory reads as periphery
summary: Kharven's Standing Inventory (permafrost, blubber lamps, weekly-counted woodpiles, no domestic coin) survives and improves, now legible as periphery — the Accord's ledgers reach Kharven, its conduit does not.
verbatim: The Standing Inventory. Kharven survives intact and improves. Permafrost, blubber lamps, woodpiles counted weekly, no coin domestically. All of that is now legible as periphery. The Accord's ledgers reach Kharven. Its conduit does not. Temür's people burn seal fat while Stannvaard burns nothing at all.
ratified: Isaac, 2026-09-12, Claude Code ruling session: the originated parts of Pack Eleven ratified with the packs already confirmed
notes: Marked proposed rather than live: depends on SS2's unconfirmed "conduit" economic model, and carries no explicit "Confirmed" marker of its own, unlike the SS1/SS3-derived SS5 rows.

title: Does a worked site recharge
summary: Whether a worked Wellspring site recharges (managed, corrupt empire) or depletes permanently (predatory, doomed empire).
verbatim: Does a worked site recharge? Permanent depletion makes the empire predatory and doomed. Recharge makes it managed and corrupt. Both are good books. Isaac's call.
ratified: Isaac, 2026-09-12, Claude Code ruling session: ruled
notes: RULED 2026-09-12: A worked site recharges: a managed, corrupt empire, not a doomed one.

title: Can a commoner buy draw
summary: Whether draw is a metered utility a commoner can buy or a guild-licence-only good, deciding whether the working class has lamps.

ratified: Isaac, 2026-09-12, Claude Code ruling session: ruled
notes: RULED 2026-09-12: No: draw is a guild-licence-only good. Commoners burn oil and tallow; the draw-hum is a sound of wealth.

title: The technology ceiling
summary: Which of rail, telegraph, print and photography exist, and which have Draw counterparts instead of mechanical ones.
verbatim: Tech ceiling. Which of rail, telegraph, print, photography exist, and which have Draw counterparts instead of mechanical ones.
ratified: Isaac, 2026-09-12, Claude Code ruling session: ruled
notes: RULED 2026-09-12: Isaac's words: 'All things that were invented from the beginning of the Victorian Era to the 1900s exist, but only from 1800-1900. No further no earlier.' Rail, telegraph, print and photography all exist mechanically; nothing post-1900.

title: Do Wells generate hostile entities, or is the site the threat
summary: Whether Wells generate hostile entities, or the site itself is the entire threat.
verbatim: Do Wells generate hostile entities, or is the site itself the entire threat?

notes: RULED 2026-09-12: Wells generate hostile entities. Against the pack's recommendation; the Bestiary gains a Well-spawn category.

title: Naming, Well versus Core versus Guild-register term

verbatim: Naming: Well versus Core versus something Guild-register. Class-marking opportunity either way.
ratified: Isaac, 2026-09-12, Claude Code ruling session: ruled
notes: RULED 2026-09-12: The common name is Core.

title: The Apparatus Rule's one-read-per-scene cap is struck

verbatim: The Apparatus Rule's one-read-per-scene cap. Struck, replaced at §4.

summary: Pack Seven's "mechanism nowhere" rule is struck.

notes: This is the corpus's known live-fire supersession target. Every Pack Seven rule row is status:superseded now that Pack Seven is extracted; most point at a more specific §1/§3/§4/§8 sibling below (see each Pack Seven row's own notes for its exact match), and the rest that have no cleaner match are backfilled into this row's supersedes list.

title: What Pack Seven got right survives the repeal
summary: The power economy remains a hard rail (finite, spent, shown on the page), the ladder remains real, and explaining a mechanism does not license a free technique; a fully explained technique that costs nothing is worse than an unexplained one.
verbatim: The economy is still a hard rail: power is finite, spent, and the spending shows on the page or it did not happen. The ladder is still real and higher is still felt before it is seen. Explaining a mechanism does not license a free one. A fully explained technique that costs nothing is worse than an unexplained one.

title: The three soft zones blanket rule struck, one exception flagged
summary: Pack Seven's three soft zones as a blanket rule are struck, with one exception flagged at §6.
verbatim: The three soft zones as a blanket rule. Struck, with one flagged exception at §6.
notes: Backfilled: supersedes R7-1-THREE_SOFT_ZONES. Exception is R12-6-RULES_AS_RULES/R12-6-MYSTIC_GRAMMAR.

title: The Mystic Register, defined
summary: The Mystic Register governs Wellsprings, sites, rites, oaths, the Veil, and anything the world does regardless of who is watching; it is stated as law, never as physics — imperative rules, prices given as prices, taboos given without justification.
verbatim: The Mystic Register governs Wellsprings, sites, rites, oaths, the Veil, and anything the world does regardless of who is watching. It is Lord of the Mysteries. It is stated as law, never as physics: rules given in the imperative, prices given as prices, taboos given without justification.
notes: Pack Fifteen §1 cites "the Mystic Register's rules stated as law, never physics clause (Twelve §6)" when striking its document-facing application (R15-1-MYSTIC_REGISTER_NEVER_PHYSICS_STRUCK) — that strike is partial (this register survives for documents that want to withhold), so no supersedes link is set here; a full supersedes would incorrectly kill this still-live definition.

title: The two registers do not mix in one passage
summary: A passage that mixes the Technical and Mystic registers reads as a textbook and is the pack's primary failure mode.
verbatim: Both registers explain. They explain differently. A passage that mixes them reads as a textbook and is the primary failure mode of this pack.

title: The test for which register a passage is in
summary: If a person chose to do a thing, it is Technical Register. If it was already running before anyone noticed, it is Mystic Register.
verbatim: The test for which register a passage is in: if a person chose to do it, Technical. If it was already running before anyone noticed, Mystic.

title: The Technical Register, defined
summary: The Technical Register governs combat, craft, injury and anything a practitioner does on purpose; exhaustive, tactical, delivered in-fight, explaining the read, the fault, the counter, the reserve and why the answer worked, in real vocabulary.
verbatim: The Technical Register governs combat, craft, injury, and anything a practitioner does on purpose. It is Naruto. It is exhaustive, tactical, and delivered in-fight. It explains the read, the fault, the counter, the reserve, and the reason the answer worked. It uses real vocabulary and does not flinch from detail.

title: The five-line card becomes a summary above the full chain
summary: Technique writeups now carry the full Design Chain in place of the old five-line format; the five-line format (Effect, Cost, Limit, Counter, What nobody knows) survives only as a summary card at the head of an entry, with the chain below it.
verbatim: Technique writeups on the page now carry the full chain in place of the five-line format. The five-line format (Effect, Cost, Limit, Counter, What nobody knows) is retained as the summary card at the head of an entry, with the chain below it.
notes: This is the five-line card format Pack Seventeen's R17-3-SIX_LINE_CARD replaces; Pack Seventeen's note flagging an unidentified five-line predecessor should be backfilled to reference this row.

title: What a combat exchange owes the reader, five minimums
summary: Across an engagement, at minimum: the read (evidence named), the fault (structural weakness), the counter and why it works (causal), the cost in body and reserve (both), and what the character cannot do next.
verbatim: What a combat exchange now owes the reader. At minimum, across the engagement:
notes: Extended and made denser by Pack Thirteen §4's eight-item combat floor (R13-4-COMBAT_FLOOR); not a supersession, Thirteen builds on this rather than striking it.

title: Every ability entry retains a mandatory Counter field
summary: Ability entries retain the Counter field as mandatory; explanation makes counterplay easier to write, not optional.
verbatim: Ability entries retain the Counter field as mandatory. Explanation makes counterplay easier to write, and it stays mandatory.
notes: Pack Seventeen's R17-3-COUNTER_MANDATORY narrows this to "mandatory on Signature techniques" specifically; a refinement, not a conflict.

title: The ten-element Design Chain is prose-legal again
summary: The Design Chain (Trigger, Function, Mechanism, Numerical Effect, Target Response, Consequence, Limitation, Weakness, Cost, Counterplay) is fully prose-legal, distributed through the scene rather than workbook-only.
verbatim: The Design Chain returns to the page. Trigger, Function, Mechanism, Numerical Effect, Target Response, Consequence, Limitation, Weakness, Cost, Counterplay. Formerly workbook-only under Pack Seven. Now prose-legal in full, distributed through the scene instead of listed.

title: Documented techniques are counterable by study; originals by live read
summary: Every technique was derived by somebody for a specific problem; a documented technique is counterable by anyone who studied it, while a self-derived technique must be read live in the exchanges before it kills, shown in full rather than summarised.
verbatim: The named inventor rule. Every technique was derived by somebody, in a specific place, for a specific problem, and the text may say so. A documented technique is counterable by anyone who studied it. A self-derived technique must be read live, in the two or three exchanges before it kills you, and the reading is now shown in full instead of summarised.

title: Explanations are characterised by class-marked vocabulary
summary: A Measurewright, a Kharven hunter and an Accord officer explain the same phenomenon in three different vocabularies; which words a mouth reaches for remains class-marking per Pack Nine.
verbatim: Voice discipline. The explanation is characterised. A Measurewright, a Kharven hunter, and an Accord officer explain the same phenomenon in three different vocabularies, and which words a mouth reaches for remains class-marking, per Pack Nine.
notes: Softened by Pack Fifteen §4 from a stricter clause to "may differ" (see R15-4-TWELVE_VOICE_DISCIPLINE_SOFTENED); a demotion, not a full strike, so no supersedes link — Pack Fifteen's amends already carries the locus §4 cross-reference.

title: Voice four: the document
summary: An in-world register entry, field manual, or codex line dropped in at a scene threshold (the LotM model), using the Mystic Register and setting a rule the scene then breaks.
verbatim: The document. The LotM model. An in-world register entry, field manual, or codex line dropped into the narrative at the threshold of a scene. Uses the Mystic Register. Sets a rule the scene then breaks.

title: Mix the four explaining voices; at most two per engagement
summary: Confirmed by Isaac's ruling: the four explaining voices may mix, whoever is in the scene, picked per scene, with no more than two run in one engagement.
verbatim: Confirmed by Isaac's ruling: mix, whoever is in the scene. Four carriers. Pick per scene. Do not run more than two in one engagement.

title: Voice one: the POV's own read
summary: Free indirect explanation ceilinged at the POV character's actual competence; an out-of-depth character explains wrong, and a confidently wrong technical explanation is now the primary vehicle for the misreading budget.
verbatim: The POV's own read. Free indirect, inside his competence. The ceiling is what this character actually knows, and a character who is out of his depth explains wrong. A wrong technical explanation delivered confidently is now the most valuable tool in the kit and replaces the misreading budget as its primary vehicle.

title: Voice three: the opponent
summary: A practitioner explains exactly what he is doing to his target while doing it, because he does not believe the explanation will help; the most economical and characterful voice, barred to anyone without standing to be arrogant.
verbatim: The opponent. Contempt as instruction. A practitioner explaining exactly what he is doing to you while doing it, because he does not believe the explanation will help. This is the most economical of the four and the most characterful, and it is barred to anyone who does not have the standing to be arrogant.

title: Voice two: the knowledgeable second
summary: A present observer who understands what the POV does not, narrating the read to a third party or himself (the Kakashi model); requires an actual reason to be present and talking, best carried by teachers, rivals, Measurewrights, or the Research and Archives Division.
verbatim: The knowledgeable second. The Kakashi model. Someone watching from outside the exchange who understands what the POV does not, narrating the read to a third party or to himself. Requires an actual reason for them to be present and talking.

title: A number is never invented
summary: Every metaphysical figure is checked against source and never invented; where unspecified, it is flagged as an estimate.
verbatim: Never invent a number. Unchanged and absolute. Every value checked against source. Unspecified means flagged as estimate.

title: Metaphysical numbers reach the page only in diagnostic voice
summary: EU, AU/s, eta, Coherence, Grade and Band numbers may not reach third-person narration on the narration's own authority; they are legal only in diagnostic voice (a faculty reading, a practitioner counting reserve, a document, an instrument, or a speaking character).
verbatim: They may not reach the narration. Numbers are legal in diagnostic voice only: a perceptive faculty actively reading, a practitioner counting his own reserve, a document, an instrument, or a character speaking. Third-person narration does not state a metaphysical figure on its own authority.
notes: This is the "Twelve §5" rationing rule Pack Fourteen §4 cites directly.

title: The grammar of the Mystic Register, five features
summary: The Mystic Register's grammar: imperative without justification, price stated exactly with no reason given, correspondence in place of causation, attribution to an uncertain institution, and the recorded failure documented in flat administrative prose.
verbatim: The grammar of the Mystic Register: - The imperative without justification. Do this, never that. - The price stated exactly and the reason for the price never. - Correspondence in place of causation. This answers to that. Nobody says why. - Attribution to an institution that is itself uncertain. The register says. The older register said otherwise. Both are filed. - The recorded failure. Somebody did it wrong once and what happened to them is documented in flat administrative prose.

title: A ritual specifies its materials, sequence and errors
summary: A rite has a fully specified bill of goods, an order of operations, and a list of ways it goes wrong.
verbatim: Ritual gets its materials, its sequence, and its errors. A rite has a bill of goods, an order of operations, and a list of ways it goes wrong, all specified.

title: Mystic Register rules are stated as rules, unexplained
summary: The Mystic Register states consequences without offering mechanism (the canonical example: do not carry Object Wellsprings into Site Wellsprings, no mechanism given, a stated consequence, the Guild has buried those who tested it); more sentences are written in that shape.
verbatim: Rules stated as rules. The strongest existing example is already canon: do not carry Object Wellsprings into Site Wellsprings. No mechanism offered, a stated consequence, and the Guild has buried the people who tested it. Write more sentences in that shape.
notes: This is the flagged exception referenced by R12-1-SOFT_ZONES_STRUCK.

title: The AI-tell checklist is retained in full
summary: The Ladder ban, the Gloss budget of zero, local burstiness, the reification budget, and every AI tell in the checklist survive unchanged; explaining a mechanism is no licence to write badly.
verbatim: Retained in full: the Ladder ban, the Gloss budget of zero, local burstiness, the reification budget, and every AI tell in the checklist. Explaining a mechanism is no licence to write badly.

title: The one-read cap is struck and replaced by a tempo cost
summary: Pack Six's Apparatus Rule one-read-per-scene cap is struck; a faculty may now read as often as the scene needs, replaced by a cost — a read occupies attention, and the scene shows what the reading cost the reader in tempo.
verbatim: Struck: the Apparatus Rule's one-read-per-scene cap. A faculty may now read as often as the scene needs. Replaced by a cost: a read occupies attention, and a character reading is a character who is doing nothing else. Show what the reading cost him in tempo.
notes: Backfilled: supersedes R6-2-ONE_READ_PER_SCENE. This is also the target for R12-1-APPARATUS_CAP_STRUCK's own backfill note, since both describe the same strike from two angles (Pack Seven's inheritance vs. Pack Six's origin).

title: The ignorance quota and misreading budget are retained, elevated
summary: The ignorance quota and misreading budget survive Pack Twelve intact and become more important as dramatic-irony tools now that explanation is the default; the wrong explanation is now the load-bearing device.
verbatim: Retained, and now more important: the ignorance quota and the misreading budget. These were never opacity tools. They are dramatic irony tools and they survive Pack Twelve intact. One thing per scene the POV cannot interpret. At least one confident inference that is wrong and stays uncorrected.

title: The total-legibility ban and zero-interpretation rule are struck
summary: Pack Six's total-legibility ban and blanket interpretation-at-zero rule are struck.
verbatim: Struck: the total-legibility ban and the blanket interpretation-at-zero rule.
notes: Backfilled: supersedes R6-5-INTERPRET_AT_ZERO_STRUCK and R6-12-TOTAL_LEGIBILITY_STRUCK.

verbatim: WOTR_Ability_Technique_Design_Guide.md. Sixth edition required. Sections 1 and 2 rewritten off §1 to §3 above. The two-ledger split is retired; there is now one ledger with a summary card. Character-first design order survives untouched and is unaffected by this pack.

verbatim: WOTR_Combat_Craft_Guide.md. The read is now shown at length, no longer summarised. The three-layer hit model is rendered as explanation and no longer only as phenomena.

verbatim: WOTR_Scene_Writing_Process_Guide.md. The Pack Seven pre-write question and self-review check are struck.

verbatim: My recommendation, pitched not decided: mechanism becomes fully explicable, and where any of it came from stays mythic. Titans, Archons, the Crevice, the Withering, Epoch-scale events. They generate dread and problems. They never resolve a plot.

title: Category is laid across all three strata
summary: The twenty-six Categories say what kind of thing came out; their alignment tag names which Plane carries the cost and which the counterplay; Category is workbook/Codex-line by default and may be named in diagnostic voice to tell the reader where to hit.
verbatim: The Category, laid across all three. The twenty-six answer what kind of thing came out. Their alignment tag (Body, Spirit, Attraction, Triadic, or a seam between two) names which Plane carries the cost and which Plane the counterplay lives on.
ratified: Isaac, 2026-09-11, Claude Code session: ratified by direction ("most of them are ratified"); his standing Natalie project instructions treat this pack as live.

title: The Craft sets durability of a projected form
summary: The Craft (per Pack Ten) is which mouth a working came out of — speaking, cutting, pouring, writing — and it sets the durability of a projected form.
verbatim: The Craft. Which mouth it came out of (Pack Ten): the speaking, the cutting, the pouring, the writing. Craft sets durability of a projected form.
ratified: Isaac, 2026-09-11, Claude Code session: ratified by direction ("most of them are ratified"); his standing Natalie project instructions treat this pack as live.

title: Stratum one: the Aether
summary: The Aether stratum is what was already in the room before a draw: Aetheric Density (AU/s ceiling), Residue, Saturation, and in the Draw Age the district main/standpipe/meter; its real-science analogue is field, gradient, reservoir, saturation, conduction, and a working changes with local density.
verbatim: Stratum one, the Aether. The ocean. Material Plane. What was in the room before anyone drew on it: Aetheric Density (sets the AU/s ceiling for that location), Aetheric Residue from prior workings, Aetheric Saturation if the room is already flooded, and in the Draw Age the district main, the standpipe, the meter, and whether the district is cut off.
ratified: Isaac, 2026-09-11, Claude Code session: ratified by direction ("most of them are ratified"); his standing Natalie project instructions treat this pack as live.

title: Stratum three: the Essence
summary: The Essence stratum is the soul's water: Soul Crystal architecture (Essence Core, Aether Shell, Attraction Layer) and cost (EU, eta, Flux Density, Crystal State); real-science analogue is efficiency, impedance, resonance, fatigue, phase change of the vessel.
verbatim: Stratum three, the Essence. The soul's water. Soul Crystal architecture: Essence Core (intent, identity), Aether Shell (conversion to force; Lattice Conductivity, Resonant Purity, Continuum Retention), Attraction Layer (recognition; Attraction Force clean, Obsession Force corrupted). Cost lives here: EU spent, eta lost as heat and static and structural bleed, Flux Density under compression, Crystal State under strain (Refined, Fractured, Overgrown, Crystallized).
ratified: Isaac, 2026-09-11, Claude Code session: ratified by direction ("most of them are ratified"); his standing Natalie project instructions treat this pack as live.

title: Stratum two: the Wellspring
summary: The Wellspring stratum is the law: each of the Sixty carries a Core Law, Family and Physics Domain assigned as real physics, and its law is stated as that real law with a directional operator; the glyph constrains degrees of freedom rather than creating the effect.
verbatim: Stratum two, the Wellspring. The law. Each of the Sixty carries a Core Law, a Family, and a Physics Domain, and the Codex assigns the Physics Domain as real physics: Thermodynamics, Electromagnetism, Mechanics, Spatial Geometry, Material Science, Biochemistry, Fluid Dynamics, Abstract/Entropic Systems, Cross-Family Boundary Physics. The Wellspring's law is stated as that real law with a directional operator on it.
ratified: Isaac, 2026-09-11, Claude Code session: ratified by direction ("most of them are ratified"); his standing Natalie project instructions treat this pack as live.

title: Every working is explained at three strata
summary: Every working explained on the page is explained at three strata (the Aether, the Wellspring, the Essence), in the Technical Register, through one of Pack Twelve's four voices; the strata's causal order need not be the order on the page.
verbatim: Every working explained on the page is explained at three strata, in the Technical Register, through one of Twelve's four voices. The order below is the order of causation. It does not have to be the order on the page.
ratified: Isaac, 2026-09-11, Claude Code session: ratified by direction ("most of them are ratified"); his standing Natalie project instructions treat this pack as live.

title: The invention step, one step past the textbook

verbatim: Then the invention step. Push the phenomenon one step past where the textbook stops. Textbook physics is the floor; the technique is what a practitioner does with it that a physicist could not.
ratified: Isaac, 2026-09-11, Claude Code session: ratified by direction ("most of them are ratified"); his standing Natalie project instructions treat this pack as live.

verbatim: The Phenomenon Bank. One seed per Physics Domain, all originated, all pending. Wellspring and Category given as the assignment that fits, decided after the phenomenon, per the Ability Guide.

verbatim: Every new working, technique, or ability names, in the author notes, before it ships:
ratified: Isaac, 2026-09-11, Claude Code session: ratified by direction ("most of them are ratified"); his standing Natalie project instructions treat this pack as live.

summary: Every meaningful exchange states, in one of the four voices: measure, tempo (Vor/Nach/Indes), the named read, the fault it exposes, the mechanics of the hit, the injury by structure with ATLS-class blood loss, the Essence account at all three strata, and what the character cannot do next.
verbatim: Every meaningful exchange (a hit that lands, a first display, a counter, a change of measure that decides something) puts the following on the page, stated, in one of the four voices:
ratified: Isaac, 2026-09-11, Claude Code session: ratified by direction ("most of them are ratified"); his standing Natalie project instructions treat this pack as live.

title: Combat floor density by scene length

verbatim: Density. A duel of 2,500 words carries the full floor at first display and finisher, and items 1 to 4 at every exchange that changes the fight. A turn of 700 to 1,500 carries 1 to 4 once and 8 at close.
ratified: Isaac, 2026-09-11, Claude Code session: ratified by direction ("most of them are ratified"); his standing Natalie project instructions treat this pack as live.

title: First display and finisher carry three causal explanations
summary: At first display and finisher, physics, Essence and Hermetic correspondence must each appear as a causal sentence beside its image, not as the image alone.
verbatim: The three layers become three explanations. Physics, Essence, Hermetic correspondence: at first display and finisher each is a causal sentence beside its image, not the image alone.
ratified: Isaac, 2026-09-11, Claude Code session: ratified by direction ("most of them are ratified"); his standing Natalie project instructions treat this pack as live.

ratified: Isaac, 2026-09-11, Claude Code session: ratified by direction ("most of them are ratified"); his standing Natalie project instructions treat this pack as live.

Three elements, one sentence or one short group: [the real phenomenon, correctly named] + [the system term as its name, its boundary condition, or its address] + [what the body or the room did]. Neither element is a gloss on the other. The science is not a metaphor for the magic and the magic is not decoration on the science. A converted grief is a failed grief. - Dialogue, except in a practitioner's diagnostic voice or a document's. - The ignorance quota (Pack Six). One thing per scene the POV perceives and cannot name. Conversion never rescues it.

title: The alchemical doctrine line, and the operations it binds
summary: Reagents are the nouns, the Wellspring is the verb, and Glyphica is the grammar; any working touching Calcination, Dissolution, Coagulatio, Distillation, Sublimare or Transmutatio is bound by Alchemetrica's entries for them.
verbatim: the reagents are the nouns, the Wellspring is the verb, Glyphica is the grammar that makes the sentence lawful. It also fixes the eight Wellsprings that are simultaneously Wellspring, cosmic principle and alchemical operation, and any working that touches Calcination, Dissolution, Coagulatio, Distillation, Sublimare or Transmutatio is bound by their entries there.
ratified: Isaac, 2026-09-12, Claude Code: ratified wholesale

title: Three alchemy sources, consulted in a fixed order
summary: Alchemy design consults, in order, the Alchemical Index (what exists), Alchemetrica (doctrine), and The Real Alchemy (real-world substrate check on invented process/apparatus/reagent behaviour), loading The Provenance Doctrine, The Standing Index and The Bench of Attribution alongside them; none of the three is optional.
verbatim: Three sources, consulted in this order, and none of them optional.
ratified: Isaac, 2026-09-12, Claude Code: ratified wholesale

title: The Codex is read from the file, never from memory
summary: The Master Codex is accessed read-only via openpyxl from the actual spreadsheet file; the sheet is the authority, not Natalie's recollection of it.
verbatim: Access method: openpyxl, read-only, from /mnt/project/The_Master_Codex.xlsx. Never from memory. The sheet is the authority and Natalie's recollection of it is not.
ratified: Isaac, 2026-09-12, Claude Code: ratified wholesale

title: New Session Start step 4a, open the Master Codex
summary: Inserted between the current steps four and five of the Session Start Protocol, a new step 4a requires querying the Spell Index, Glyph Index, Alchemical Index and Lists sheet for everything the scene will work, before the FOW line and before the Standing Inventory.
verbatim: 4a. Open the Master Codex for anything the scene will work. Query the Spell Index for existing precedent, the Glyph Index for the phenomenon, the Alchemical Index for any reagent, and the Lists sheet for every assignment the scene will name. Do this before the FOW line and before the Standing Inventory, because the Codex determines what the working is and the others determine what it costs and how it reads.
ratified: Isaac, 2026-09-12, Claude Code: ratified wholesale

title: Check 37 — Controlled vocabulary
summary: Every Wellspring, Family, Physics Domain, Temperance stage, Archon, Titan, Glyph Class, alchemical Tier and Type named in a file is validated against the Lists sheet; anything absent fails unless declared as a proposed new entry naming the checked enumeration.
verbatim: Check 37 — Controlled vocabulary. Every Wellspring, Family, Physics Domain, Temperance stage, Archon, Titan, Glyph Class, alchemical Tier and alchemical Type named in the file is validated against the Lists sheet. Anything absent is a FAIL and must be either corrected or explicitly declared as a proposed new entry with the checked enumeration named.
ratified: Isaac, 2026-09-12, Claude Code: ratified wholesale

title: Check 38 — Glyph validity
summary: Every bracketed glyph token in a file is validated against the Master Glyph Index; unknown tokens fail.
verbatim: Check 38 — Glyph validity. Every bracketed glyph token in the file is validated against the Master Glyph Index. Unknown tokens FAIL.
ratified: Isaac, 2026-09-12, Claude Code: ratified wholesale

title: Check 39 — Precedent
summary: Manual check: for any new working, name the Spell Index rows checked and state whether the working is new, a derivation of a named row, or a duplicate.
verbatim: Check 39 — Precedent. Manual. For any new working, name the Spell Index rows checked and state whether the working is new, a derivation of a named row, or a duplicate.
ratified: Isaac, 2026-09-12, Claude Code: ratified wholesale

title: Standing task, fold amendments into base guides
summary: Fold Packs One through Eighteen into the base guides and retire the diffs, asked once per session.
verbatim: Fold Packs One through Eighteen into the base guides and retire the diffs. Ask once per session.
ratified: Isaac, 2026-09-12, Claude Code: ratified wholesale

title: Prose is built around fixed dialogue, not the reverse
summary: Scenes are constructed to make Isaac's fixed lines land; the dialogue is never fitted to prose written ahead of it.
verbatim: The prose is built around the dialogue, never over it. Isaac's lines are the fixed points and the scene is constructed to make them land.
ratified: Isaac, 2026-09-12, Claude Code: ratified wholesale

title: Isaac's dialogue is fixed text
summary: Isaac's submitted dialogue is set as written and never rewritten.
verbatim: Set it. Do not rewrite it.
ratified: Isaac, 2026-09-12, Claude Code: ratified wholesale
notes: Extends Pack Sixteen's vocabulary-conversion principle (§1) from vocabulary to speech generally; not a supersession of Pack Sixteen, which is not named as struck or replaced anywhere in this pack.

title: What may never be altered in Isaac's dialogue
summary: Register, rhythm, repetition, fragments, profanity, prosodic marks, line order, and word choice in Isaac's dialogue may never be changed, including for the sake of reading better.
verbatim: May never be altered: - Register, diction or formality level - Rhythm, sentence length, or clause structure - Repetition, including repetition that looks accidental - Fragments, run-ons, missing conjunctions - Profanity, crudeness, or bluntness of any kind - Capitals, stretched vowels, ellipses, and every other prosodic mark (see §3) - The order in which a character says things - Anything at all on the grounds that it reads better the other way
ratified: Isaac, 2026-09-12, Claude Code: ratified wholesale

title: The narrow set of silent corrections to Isaac's dialogue
summary: Only typos, unambiguous verb tense/agreement, required punctuation, and stale canon-term forms may be silently corrected in Isaac's dialogue.
verbatim: May be corrected silently: - Typographical slips and dropped words (wsaas → was) - Verb tense and agreement where the intent is unambiguous - Punctuation required for the line to parse - A canon term used in a stale or incorrect form (Khavern → Kharven, kurotesu → Kurosetsu)
ratified: Isaac, 2026-09-12, Claude Code: ratified wholesale

title: Procedure when a fixed line breaks canon
summary: A canon-breaking line in Isaac's dialogue is flagged once in author notes and left standing, untouched, unless Isaac rules otherwise.
verbatim: Where a line genuinely breaks the world — a term that contradicts canon, a name that has been retired, a claim that cannot be true — Natalie flags it in one sentence in the author notes and leaves the line standing unless Isaac rules otherwise. The draft is not touched.
ratified: Isaac, 2026-09-12, Claude Code: ratified wholesale

title: Prosodic marks are reproduced verbatim, never normalised
summary: Capitals, stretched vowels, ellipses and repeated punctuation are notation for volume, duration, breath and intensity, and must be reproduced exactly rather than converted into narrative description.
verbatim: Natalie does not convert stretched vowels into a narrative tag (he tore it out of himself), does not reduce capitals to italics, and does not tidy ellipses into em dashes or commas.
ratified: Isaac, 2026-09-12, Claude Code: ratified wholesale

title: A descriptive tag may accompany prosody, never replace it
summary: A narrative tag may be added next to prosodic notation but may never be used instead of it.
verbatim: A tag may be added alongside prosody. It may never be added instead of it.
ratified: Isaac, 2026-09-12, Claude Code: ratified wholesale

title: Staying composed under stress must cost visibly
summary: A character who stays composed under extreme stress is exercising an expensive discipline, and the scene must show that price.
verbatim: The inverse is a character note and it must cost. A character who does stay composed under extreme stress is exercising an expensive discipline, and the scene shows the price.
ratified: Isaac, 2026-09-12, Claude Code: ratified wholesale

title: The iceberg rule applies to dialogue
summary: Characters never explain to each other something they both already know.
verbatim: And nobody explains anything they both already know. The iceberg rule is a dialogue rule first.
ratified: Isaac, 2026-09-12, Claude Code: ratified wholesale

title: Originated dialogue must show real-time speech production
summary: Originated dialogue must include false starts and self-repair, interruption, repetition, non-answers, characters talking past each other, trailing off, physical business mid-line, and characters saying the wrong thing, as craft law rather than optional flavour.
verbatim: Speech is not prose. It is produced in real time by a person who has not finished thinking.
ratified: Isaac, 2026-09-12, Claude Code: ratified wholesale
notes: Source lists eight specific artefacts (false starts/self-repair, interruption, repetition, non-answers, talking past each other, trailing off, physical business mid-line, saying the wrong thing) under one craft-law header; kept as one row rather than eight since the source treats them as one checklist, not eight separately verified rules.

title: Register under stress shortens and simplifies
summary: Under stress, a character's speech must get shorter, more concrete, more repetitive, and lose subordinate clauses, uniformly across all characters.
verbatim: Register moves with state, and it moves the same way in every human being. Under stress, speech gets shorter, more concrete, more repetitive, and loses subordinate clauses.
ratified: Isaac, 2026-09-12, Claude Code: ratified wholesale

title: Speech idiom is anchored to the speaker's own life
summary: A character's metaphors and idiom must come from their own life and trade, not from an external reference list.
verbatim: Speech is world-anchored. People reach for the objects and idioms their life has given them.
ratified: Isaac, 2026-09-12, Claude Code: ratified wholesale

title: The composure ban
summary: Bars antithesis and parallelism, three-part lists, long subordinate clauses in shouted speech, and perfect syntax from established inarticulate/young/exhausted/foreign characters, and bars every character in a scene from constructing sentences at the same length.
verbatim: No character speaks in balanced clauses under duress, and Natalie's habit of writing everyone that way is a tell.
ratified: Isaac, 2026-09-12, Claude Code: ratified wholesale
notes: Source itemises five specific bars under this header (antithesis under duress, three-part lists from bleeding/frightened/grieving characters, subordinate clauses over ~11 words in shouted speech, perfect syntax from characters established as inarticulate/young/exhausted/foreign, and uniform sentence length across a scene's speakers); kept as one row since they are one named ban, not five independently checked ones.

title: The cover-the-tags test is now a Pack Nineteen failure
summary: If a stranger could not sort a scene's dialogue lines by speaker with the tags covered, the scene fails as a Pack Nineteen violation, not merely a voice-differentiation warning.
verbatim: Cover the dialogue tags and read the lines. If a stranger could not sort them by speaker, the scene failed, and the failure is now a Pack Nineteen failure and not merely a voice-differentiation warning.
ratified: Isaac, 2026-09-12, Claude Code: ratified wholesale
notes: Escalates the severity of the existing voice-differentiation test (compare R15-1-VOICE_DIFFERENTIATION) rather than replacing it; no supersedes link, since nothing is struck.

title: Check 40 — Fidelity
summary: Manual check that every line of Isaac's dialogue matches the submitted rough verbatim except for corrections permitted in §2; any other change fails and is reverted.
verbatim: Check 40 — Fidelity. Manual. Diff the output against the submitted rough. Every line of Isaac's dialogue appears verbatim except for the corrections permitted in §2. Any other change is a FAIL and is reverted.
ratified: Isaac, 2026-09-12, Claude Code: ratified wholesale

title: Check 41 — Prosody
summary: Automatic check that fails when the submitted rough has stretched vowels, repeated punctuation or capitalised shouting that the output drops.
verbatim: Check 41 — Prosody. Automatic where possible. If the submitted rough contains stretched vowels, repeated punctuation or capitalised shouting and the output does not, FAIL.
ratified: Isaac, 2026-09-12, Claude Code: ratified wholesale

title: Check 42 — Composure
summary: Flags long, subordinate-heavy or parallel dialogue lines and reports the spread of line lengths across a scene, flagging files where every speaker clusters at one length.
verbatim: Check 42 — Composure. Flags dialogue lines that are long, subordinate-heavy, or contain parallel constructions, and reports the spread of line lengths across the scene.
ratified: Isaac, 2026-09-12, Claude Code: ratified wholesale

title: The pack is not retroactive
summary: No rewrite of scenes written before this pack is proposed; the pack governs dialogue written from here forward.
verbatim: No rewrite of past scenes is proposed. The pack governs from here.
ratified: Isaac, 2026-09-12, Claude Code: ratified wholesale

summary: Fold Packs One through Nineteen into the base guides and retire the diffs, asked once per session.
verbatim: Fold Packs One through Nineteen into the base guides and retire the diffs. Ask once per session.
